cancel.howTo: Cancel in the Greenlight app or on the website under the parent account and plan settings, or contact support. Move balances out of the kids accounts first, since closing the plan will likely close the cards.
cancel.gotchas: Greenlight's help center lists Core at $5.99 a month, Max at $10.98, Infinity at $15.98 and Family Shield at $19.98, per family rather than per child. A custom card is a one-time $9.99.

name: Habitify
why: A habit tracker is the textbook personal rebuild: checklist, streaks, calendar, local data. You give up cross-device sync and polish. The free plan covers up to 3 habits, which may be enough.

alternatives.name: Loop Habit Tracker (Android)
alternatives.note: Open-source habit tracker for Android; data stays on the device.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: An installable habit tracker with scheduled habits, numeric goals, a one-tap today screen, streaks and a calendar heatmap, weekly reviews, and optional reminders.
rebuild.runsOn: Installable PWA on your phone home screen; data in IndexedDB on the device; hosted free on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages.
rebuild.youLose: Habitify's sync across devices, Apple Watch and widgets, Apple Health integration, and its polished reminders. Web notifications are less reliable on iPhone.
rebuild.prompt: Build a personal habit tracker as an installable PWA (React, Vite, TypeScript, IndexedDB, no backend). Features: (1) habits with a schedule (daily, specific weekdays, or N times per week), optional numeric goals such as 8 glasses of water, and time-of-day grouping; (2) one-tap check-in from a Today screen, with skip and note options; (3) streaks, completion rate and a calendar heatmap per habit; (4) weekly and monthly review charts; (5) local reminders using the Notifications API where the browser supports them, with a clear fallback message where it does not; (6) archive and reorder habits. Keep all data in IndexedDB with JSON and CSV export and import. Check whether Habitify can export my history and, if so, write an importer after confirming its columns with me. Make it offline-first, dark-mode aware and keyboard accessible, add tests for the streak logic, and finish with free deploy steps for GitHub Pages.

cancel.howTo: Cancel where you subscribed. For web purchases, Habitify payments go through Paddle: open the Paddle receipt email and use its link to manage the payment. For in-app purchases use the App Store or Google Play subscription list. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: The help center says Pro Monthly carries a 12-month commitment on iOS, so cancelling mid-year may not stop the remaining charges the way you expect. Plus is annual only. Several price points exist across stores, so read the renewal amount in your subscription list. Export first from Settings > Import / Export (CSV, in newer app versions) and check the file. Keep the paid plan until the import is verified.

name: Happier Meditation (Ten Percent Happier)
why: Course-based teaching content you finish and move on from. Pay monthly while you work through a course, cancel, and return for the next one. Annual only pays if you use it most of the year.

alternatives.name: Insight Timer (free)
alternatives.note: Free timer and a large library of guided meditations.

alternatives.name: Smiling Mind
alternatives.note: Free guided mindfulness programs from a nonprofit.

rotate.pattern: Subscribe monthly ($14.99) when you start a course, finish it, cancel, and come back for the next. Six months of monthly billing is about the same as the $99.99 annual plan, so rotation pays only if you stay off 6 or more months.

cancel.howTo: Cancel in the App Store or Google Play subscription list, where the app now appears as "Happier: Meditation". If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: The app was renamed, so search for "Happier" in your subscription list. The App Store lists several price points ($59.99 to $99.99 a year), so read the renewal price shown there.

name: Headspace
why: Guided meditation audio is content you rent, and free apps cover the basics. Pay monthly only in the stretches you use it, then cancel; if you open it just a few times a month, cancel outright.

alternatives.name: Insight Timer (free)
alternatives.note: Free timer and a large library of guided meditations.

alternatives.name: Smiling Mind
alternatives.note: Free guided mindfulness programs from a nonprofit.

rotate.pattern: Pay the $12.99 monthly plan only in stressful or sleep-poor stretches, cancel when they pass, and use a free app in between. This pays only if you are on the monthly plan: the $69.99 annual plan is cheaper unless you stay off 7 or more months a year.

cancel.howTo: If you subscribed on headspace.com, log in and open subscription management to cancel; if the button is missing, email help@headspace.com. On iPhone use Settings > your name > Subscriptions; on Android use Google Play. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: Subscriptions bought directly from Headspace are generally non-refundable, though the help center says special cases are reviewed by email. Promotional first-year prices can renew at the regular rate, so check the renewal amount before the first anniversary. Headspace coaching and therapy are separate, higher-priced products.

name: Huckleberry
why: Baby tracking is the textbook rebuild: timers, summaries and a nap predictor. You lose Huckleberry's SweetSpot-quality predictions, the sleep plans and easy multi-caregiver sync.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: An installable baby tracker with one-tap sleep, feed, diaper and pumping timers, a daily timeline and weekly summaries, an editable age-based nap predictor, and a doctor-visit summary export.
rebuild.runsOn: Installable PWA on your phone home screen; data in IndexedDB on the device; hosted free on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages.
rebuild.youLose: Huckleberry's SweetSpot predictions trained on many babies, its personalized sleep plans and AI guidance, and effortless multi-caregiver sync. Sharing is by export file, not live sync.
rebuild.prompt: Build a baby sleep and feeding tracker as an installable PWA (React, Vite, TypeScript, IndexedDB, no backend). Features: (1) one-tap timers for sleep, breast or bottle feeds, diapers and pumping, with editing and backdating; (2) a today timeline plus daily and weekly summaries (total sleep, longest stretch, feeds, diapers); (3) a nap predictor that suggests the next sleep window from age-based wake-window ranges that I can edit, narrowing as it learns from my baby last ten days; (4) a shareable summary exported as a PNG or text for a pediatrician visit or caregiver; (5) multiple children; (6) a dim red night mode. Store data locally with JSON and CSV export and import, and add a Huckleberry importer if its data export can be downloaded (inspect it first and ask me about column mapping). Include tests for the predictor, offline support, and free deploy steps for Cloudflare Pages.

cancel.howTo: In the Huckleberry app: Settings (gear icon) > Huckleberry Memberships > Cancel subscription. If you subscribed through the App Store or Google Play, cancel in that store's subscription list instead; if you bought on the Huckleberry website, use the link in your receipt. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: Cancel at least 24 hours before the next billing date. Deleting or uninstalling the app does not cancel, and cancelling does not automatically refund. Huckleberry lists Premium at $14.99 monthly or $9.99 a month billed yearly, and Plus at $11.99 monthly or $5.74 a month billed yearly. Export first: tap the child icon, then Export tracking data as CSV. The emailed link expires in 24 hours and covers one child per export, so repeat it for each child. Keep the paid plan until the import is verified.

name: Insight Timer Plus (MemberPlus)
why: The free tier already includes the timer and a large meditation library. MemberPlus adds extras such as a challenge archive, custom folders and journaling tools that most people use rarely.

alternatives.name: Insight Timer (free)
alternatives.note: Free timer and a large library of guided meditations.

alternatives.name: Smiling Mind
alternatives.note: Free guided mindfulness programs from a nonprofit.

cancel.howTo: Turn off auto-renew in the App Store or Google Play subscription list, or in your Insight Timer account if you subscribed on the web. Do it at least 24 hours before renewal; you keep access until the period ends. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: Unused portions of a subscription are not refunded. A 7-day free trial converts to paid unless you cancel in time. Annual is $59.99 against $9.99 monthly.

name: Ladder
why: You pay for coach-designed weekly plans with audio cueing, video demos and a team. Claude can write a program but not that structure. Keep it if the plan keeps you training; annual is half the monthly price.

alternatives.name: Hevy
alternatives.note: Workout logger with a free tier; check current free-tier limits.

cancel.howTo: Cancel in the App Store subscription list if you subscribed in the iOS app, or contact support@joinladder.com if you subscribed on the web. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: Pro Annual is $179.99 billed once, against $29.99 monthly. Ladder's 7-day trial needs no credit card, so a charge means you subscribed after it. Check whether Apple or Ladder bills you, and switch to annual only if you will train for most of the year.

name: Life360
why: A location circle holds other people's data and works only if everyone uses the same app. Keep a paid tier for longer history and emergency dispatch; if you only share location, the free plan or built-in sharing may do.

alternatives.name: Apple Find My
alternatives.note: Free location sharing between Apple devices.

alternatives.name: Google Family Link
alternatives.note: Free location and screen-time tools for Android family groups.

cancel.howTo: In the Life360 app, open Settings and the membership section to manage or cancel; if you are billed through Apple or Google, cancel in the App Store or Play Store. Cancelling returns the circle to the free plan. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: Silver, Gold and Platinum are listed at $9.99, $16.99 and $24.99 a month on Life360's site, with a discount for annual billing, and the App Store lists the same monthly prices. Check which tier your charge matches.

name: Lose It Premium
why: A daily calorie budget, food log, barcode scan and weight trend is a weekend build on open food data. You lose Lose It's database depth and the community, and Premium is only about $40 a year.

alternatives.name: Cronometer (free plan)
alternatives.note: Free plan logs food, scans barcodes and uses a verified food database.

alternatives.name: Open Food Facts
alternatives.note: Free, open food database with barcode lookup; coverage is uneven for restaurant and store-brand items.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: An installable calorie-budget tracker: goal weight and weekly rate set a daily budget, with a food log, barcode scan, exercise credit, and a weight trend with a projected goal date.
rebuild.runsOn: Installable PWA on your phone home screen; data in IndexedDB on the device; hosted free on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages.
rebuild.youLose: Lose It's large branded-food database and its community challenges, plus Apple Health and fitness-device syncing and phone-to-laptop sync. Open Food Facts covers packaged foods unevenly.
rebuild.prompt: Build a personal calorie-budget tracker as an installable PWA (React, Vite, TypeScript, IndexedDB, no backend). Features: (1) set a goal weight and weekly rate, then compute a daily calorie budget from my weight, height, age and activity level using Mifflin-St Jeor; (2) a fast food log by meal with search over Open Food Facts and USDA FoodData Central (I will paste a free USDA API key into settings), custom foods, and recent and frequent items; (3) barcode scanning through the camera using @zxing/browser; (4) an exercise log that adds calories back to the day; (5) weight entries with a trend line and projected goal date; (6) a weekly summary screen with streaks. Tell me to export my Lose It data before I cancel Premium, then write an importer after inspecting the file columns and confirming the mapping with me. Everything stays on my device with JSON and CSV backup. Work offline, keep the UI quick for one-handed use, add unit tests for the budget math, and give me free deploy steps for GitHub Pages.

cancel.howTo: Cancel in the App Store or Google Play if you subscribed there, or in your Lose It account on the website if you subscribed directly. Premium stays active through the paid period. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: Lifetime purchases exist and are not subscriptions, so check the Apple Subscriptions list before assuming you are billed yearly. Free trials convert to paid unless cancelled at least 24 hours before the end. Export your food, weight and exercise logs from the Lose It website (account settings) while Premium is active; some export options have been Premium-only. Keep the paid plan until the import is verified.

name: MyFitnessPal Premium
why: The core job is a food and weight diary. A personal PWA on USDA and Open Food Facts data covers it for free; you lose the huge crowd-sourced food database and app integrations.

alternatives.name: Cronometer (free plan)
alternatives.note: Free plan logs food, scans barcodes and uses a verified food database.

alternatives.name: Open Food Facts
alternatives.note: Free, open food database with barcode lookup; coverage is uneven for restaurant and store-brand items.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: An installable food and weight diary: log foods by meal with calories and macros, scan barcodes, save meals, track weight with a trend line, and see daily targets.
rebuild.runsOn: Installable PWA on your phone home screen; data in IndexedDB on the device; hosted free on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages.
rebuild.youLose: MyFitnessPal's crowd-sourced food database is far larger than open data, which is patchier for store brands and restaurants. You also lose Apple Health and device syncs, friends, and phone-to-laptop sync.
rebuild.prompt: Build me a free personal food diary as an installable PWA (React, Vite, TypeScript, no backend, no accounts). Core features: (1) daily log by meal with calories, protein, carbs and fat; (2) food search against the USDA FoodData Central API (I will paste a free API key into settings) and Open Food Facts for packaged foods, plus a small bundled starter list so it works before the key is set; (3) barcode scanning with the phone camera using @zxing/browser, looking up Open Food Facts; (4) saved meals and custom foods; (5) a weight log with a 7-day moving-average chart; (6) calorie and macro targets with a daily progress ring. Store everything in IndexedDB, add JSON and CSV export and import, and tell me to export my MyFitnessPal data (Premium only) before I cancel, then write an importer for the CSV, inspecting its columns first and confirming the mapping with me. Work offline after first load. Deploy free to GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages and write a README. Propose the data model first, then build in small tested steps.

cancel.howTo: Cancel in the app under Settings (Premium), or in the App Store or Google Play if you signed up there. Premium stays active until the end of the paid period. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: The 7-day free trial auto-renews unless canceled at least 24 hours before the renewal date. Annual billing is $79.99 against $19.99 monthly, so check which one you are on. Cancelling leaves a limited free tier, not a deleted account. Export first: on the website go to Reports > Export Data while Premium is active. The bulk export (a zip of CSV files sent by email) is a Premium feature. Keep the paid plan until the import is verified.

name: Noom
why: Noom bills the whole multi-month plan upfront and auto-renews. Most people get the habit lessons in a few months, then a free logger does the rest. End it on purpose, or ask for a renewal discount.

alternatives.name: Cronometer (free plan)
alternatives.note: Free plan logs food, scans barcodes and uses a verified food database.

alternatives.name: Open Food Facts
alternatives.note: Free, open food database with barcode lookup; coverage is uneven for restaurant and store-brand items.

haggle.leverage: Plans auto-renew and can be cancelled at any time, so you can credibly say you are about to leave. Free food loggers (Cronometer, MyFitnessPal free tier) are real alternatives. Retention offers are reported by third parties but are not guaranteed.
haggle.script: Hi, my Noom plan is about to renew and I am deciding whether to continue. I have been using it for a while, and at the current price I am leaning toward switching to a free food-logging app. Before I cancel, is there a discounted renewal rate or a lower-priced plan you can offer? I would stay at a price closer to [target price]. If you can offer something, please confirm the new price, the length of the term, and the next billing date in writing before I accept.
haggle.bestTime: A few days before the plan renews, through the in-app cancel flow or support chat. Not during the trial.

cancel.howTo: Cancel in the Noom app (profile picture > Settings > Manage Subscription), on the web through the Subscription Portal (Cancel Subscription), or in the App Store or Google Play if you subscribed there. Uninstalling the app does not cancel. Cancel before a trial ends to avoid the first charge.
cancel.gotchas: Plans are billed upfront for the whole term and auto-renew. Noom lists, for new accounts from March 31, 2026, $70 for one month, $169 for 4 months and $209 for a year. The trial price you pick is separate from the plan. Noom Med and GLP-1 programs are clinical and billed separately: talk to your prescriber before stopping any medication.

name: Oura Membership
why: The ring works without a membership but with far fewer insights, and the models behind them are Oura's. There is nothing to rebuild. Keep it while you use the insights; you can export your data as CSV any time.

cancel.howTo: Cancel anytime in the Membership Hub on ouraring.com. You keep full access until the end of the current billing cycle, and your data stays saved unless you delete the account.
cancel.gotchas: The ring and app keep working without a membership, but with far fewer insights. You can export your data as CSV from the Membership Hub even without a membership. Membership is $5.99 a month or $69.99 a year, and new members get the first month free.

name: Peloton App

examples: PELOTON INTERACTIVE INC NEW YORK NY

why: Classes are licensed content you can rent by the season. Pay month to month for a training block, cancel for the outdoor months, and skip the annual plan unless you use it most of the year.

rotate.pattern: Subscribe month to month while you follow a class series, cancel when it ends or when you move outdoors, and restart when you want classes again. The App Store lists App One at $15.99 a month or $159 a year, so rotation beats the annual plan only if you stay off 3 or more months.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at onepeloton.com, open Membership and cancel the App membership. If you subscribed through the App Store or Google Play, cancel there. Member Support at support.onepeloton.com can help. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: Downgrading between App plans takes effect at the end of the billing cycle with no refund. The free trial needs a card and bills automatically. The App Store lists App One at $15.99 a month and App+ at $28.99 a month. A charge much larger than these is probably the All-Access membership that comes with a Peloton bike, tread or row, which this card does not cover.

name: RISE Sleep (Rise Science)
why: Sleep debt and an energy schedule are arithmetic on your sleep log, and Apple Health can export it. A personal tool covers the core; you lose automatic sleep detection and the tuned circadian model.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: An installable sleep-debt tracker: log sleep manually or import an Apple Health export, estimate your sleep need, show 14-night sleep debt, and give a simple daily energy schedule and tonight's bedtime suggestion.
rebuild.runsOn: Installable PWA on your phone home screen; data in IndexedDB on the device; hosted free on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages.
rebuild.youLose: RISE's automatic sleep detection from your phone and wearables, its circadian model refined on many users, and nudges. Importing from Apple Health is a manual file upload, not a live sync.
rebuild.prompt: Build a sleep debt and energy tracker as an installable PWA (React, Vite, TypeScript, IndexedDB, no backend). Features: (1) log bedtime and wake time manually, or import from my Apple Health export: I upload export.zip, you unzip it in the browser with fflate and stream-parse export.xml in a Web Worker, keeping HKCategoryTypeIdentifierSleepAnalysis asleep records; (2) estimate my personal sleep need as the median sleep on days I wake without an alarm, with a manual override; (3) a sleep debt number over the last 14 nights, with a chart; (4) a simple daily energy schedule showing a morning peak, an afternoon dip and an evening wind-down window, computed from wake time and a chronotype offset I can adjust; (5) a suggested bedtime tonight to chip away at the debt. Add JSON export and import, tests for the debt math, offline support, and free deploy steps for GitHub Pages. Explain the formulas in the README, and say clearly in the UI that this is a planning aid, not medical advice.

cancel.howTo: Cancel in the App Store or Google Play subscription list, since RISE is sold through the stores. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: The yearly plan starts with a 7-day free trial that converts to $69.99 a year unless you cancel at least 24 hours before it ends. Company materials also mention monthly and lifetime options, so check which one you hold. RISE documents no export of its own history. It reads sleep from Apple Health or Health Connect, so export Apple Health (Health app > profile picture > Export All Health Data) before you cancel or delete the app. Keep the paid plan until the import is verified.

name: Sleep Cycle Premium
why: The smart alarm and sleep analysis rely on microphone access and background running that a web app cannot match. Keep it if you use the alarm; otherwise the free version is the cheaper option.

cancel.howTo: Cancel in the App Store or Google Play subscription list, since Premium is sold through the stores. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: Its App Store page lists many Premium price points, including $9.99 and $39.99 items, so the annual price is not fixed; read the renewal price in your subscription list. The trial converts to paid unless cancelled in time.

name: Strava
why: Segments, heatmaps and your friends feed are a network and a data service, not something to rebuild. The free tier still records and shares activities, so pay only if you use the paid analysis.

cancel.howTo: Cancel on the platform where you subscribed: your Strava account page if you subscribed on strava.com, or your App Store or Google Play subscription list. Your subscription renews unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the renewal date. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: Annual is $79.99 against $11.99 monthly, so a monthly plan costs about 80 percent more over a year. Canceling a recent renewal does not start a refund by itself; Strava says website purchases may be refundable within 14 days. Cancelling keeps your activities and the free feed; you lose paid analysis and routes at the end of the period.

name: Talkspace
why: Therapy is clinical care, so nothing here is rebuilt or replaced by Claude. Keep it if it helps. Messaging therapy is covered by many insurance plans, which can cut the cost sharply.

alternatives.name: Open Path Collective
alternatives.note: Sliding-scale therapy sessions; check current fees.

cancel.howTo: Cancel from your Talkspace account settings or by contacting Talkspace support. Out-of-pocket members can pause for up to seven days. Unused live sessions expire after 30 days.
cancel.gotchas: Out-of-pocket plans bill weekly: messaging $69, video plus messaging from $99, premium from $109. The $299 monthly figure here is the messaging plan averaged over a month. Check whether your insurance covers it before paying out of pocket. If you are in active treatment, tell your therapist before stopping, ask for a handoff or referral, and call or text 988 in a crisis.

name: WeightWatchers

examples: WW INTERNATIONAL INC NEW YORK NY

why: WW plans renew automatically, and the price you joined at may not be the renewal price. Ask for a retention offer before the term ends, or cancel and use a free food logger.

alternatives.name: Cronometer (free plan)
alternatives.note: Free plan logs food, scans barcodes and uses a verified food database.

alternatives.name: Open Food Facts
alternatives.note: Free, open food database with barcode lookup; coverage is uneven for restaurant and store-brand items.

haggle.leverage: WW plans renew automatically, so you hold the cancel decision, and free food loggers are a credible alternative. Retention offers are common in subscription cancel flows but are not guaranteed.
haggle.script: Hello, I am a WW member and my plan renews soon. I am considering cancelling and using a free tracking app instead. Is there a loyalty or retention rate that keeps me at or below my current monthly price? If so, please confirm the exact monthly price, whether it starts a new commitment, and the renewal date in writing before I agree. If not, please tell me how to cancel before the renewal date.
haggle.bestTime: A few weeks before your plan renews, by phone or chat, so cancellation is still possible before auto-renewal.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at weightwatchers.com or the WW app and use the membership settings to cancel, or contact member support. If you joined through the App Store or Google Play, cancel there. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: Check your plan terms for any minimum commitment and the renewal date, and put that date in your calendar. The renewal price can differ from the sign-up rate. Med+ is a clinical program with medication costs billed separately: talk to your prescriber before stopping any medication.

name: WHOOP Membership
why: The membership is the product: the strap works only with it, and the analysis runs on WHOOP's servers. There is nothing to rebuild, and the Life tier adds a heart screener. Cancel only if you stop wearing it.

cancel.howTo: Manage or cancel the membership in the WHOOP app (account and membership settings) or in your WHOOP account on the web. The WHOOP support site has the pause and cancel policy.
cancel.gotchas: WHOOP's site lists memberships at $199 (One), $239 (Peak) and $359 (Life) a year. Ask what happens to the device if you cancel before the term ends, and check the terms before switching tiers.

name: YAZIO Pro
why: A food diary, fasting timer and recipe book is a weekend build on Open Food Facts. You lose Yazio's curated database, ready-made meal plans and polish; Pro is under $50 a year.

alternatives.name: Open Food Facts
alternatives.note: Free, open food database with barcode lookup; coverage is uneven for restaurant and store-brand items.

alternatives.name: Cronometer (free plan)
alternatives.note: Free plan logs food, scans barcodes and uses a verified food database.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: An installable nutrition diary with a fasting timer, a recipe book that computes per-serving nutrition, weight tracking and a simple weekly meal planner.
rebuild.runsOn: Installable PWA on your phone home screen; data in IndexedDB on the device; hosted free on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages.
rebuild.youLose: Yazio's curated food database, ready-made recipes and meal plans, and its coaching content. Barcode coverage depends on Open Food Facts, and there is no sync between devices.
rebuild.prompt: Build me a free personal nutrition and fasting tracker as an installable PWA (React, Vite, TypeScript, IndexedDB, no server). Core features: (1) a daily food diary with calories and macros, using Open Food Facts search and barcode scanning via @zxing/browser; (2) an intermittent fasting timer with presets 16:8, 18:6 and 5:2, history, and a local notification when the eating window opens or closes where the browser supports it; (3) a recipe book where I enter ingredients once and it computes per-serving nutrition and can add the recipe to the diary; (4) a weight and measurements log with a trend chart; (5) a weekly meal planner that sums each day. Offer JSON export and import for backup. Tell me to request my Yazio data export before I cancel, then write an importer after inspecting its format with me. Keep it offline-capable, accessible and fast. Include tests for the nutrition math and a README with free deploy steps for Cloudflare Pages.

cancel.howTo: Cancel where you subscribed: the App Store or Google Play subscription list, or the cancellation form at yazio.com/en/app/account/cancel if you bought Pro on the website. Deleting the app does not stop billing. You keep Pro until the paid period ends. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: Canceling does not trigger a refund, and you cannot pause or shorten an active term. Intro offers can be priced below the regular 12-month rate ($47.90 in the App Store), so check the renewal amount in your Apple Subscriptions screen. Yazio's in-app export is limited, so ask Yazio for your full data in writing (a data access request) and wait for the file before you cancel. Keep the paid plan until the import is verified.

name: Zero (Fasting)
why: A fasting timer with history and streaks is a few hours of work. Rebuild it, keep the data on your phone, and give up only Zero's content and stage visuals.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: An installable fasting tracker with a circular timer, presets and custom windows, editable history, streaks, weekly charts, and optional weight and mood notes.
rebuild.runsOn: Installable PWA on your phone home screen; data in IndexedDB on the device; hosted free on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages.
rebuild.youLose: Zero's guided content, its stage illustrations and community, and cross-device sync. Browser notifications are less reliable than a native app, especially on iPhone.
rebuild.prompt: Build an intermittent fasting tracker as an installable PWA (React, Vite, TypeScript, IndexedDB, no backend). Features: (1) start and end a fast with a large circular timer, plus presets 12:12, 16:8, 18:6, 20:4 and a custom length; (2) edit start and end times after the fact; (3) fasting stage labels (fed, early fasting, fat burning, ketosis) shown as rough guides with a note that they are generalizations and not medical advice; (4) history with streaks, average fast length and a weekly bar chart; (5) optional weight and mood notes per fast; (6) local notifications for the planned end time where the browser supports them, with a clear fallback message where it does not. Keep data in IndexedDB with JSON and CSV export and import, and tell me to export my Zero history before I cancel, so you can add an importer after confirming the columns with me. Work offline, add tests for duration and streak logic, and finish with free deploy steps for Cloudflare Pages.

cancel.howTo: Cancel in the App Store or Google Play subscription list, since Zero Plus is sold through the stores. If you subscribed through the App Store: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel Subscription. If through Google Play: Play Store > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > the app > Cancel.
cancel.gotchas: The App Store lists Zero Plus at several price points, from $19.99 to $89.99, so read the renewal amount in your subscription list. Check the renewal date, since trials convert to paid unless cancelled. Export your fasting history from the app first (Zero lists a spreadsheet export) and check the file before you cancel. Keep the paid plan until the import is verified.

name: Bear Pro
why: Bear Pro is mostly iCloud sync plus export and locking, for $29.99 a year. If you only use one Apple device, the free app is enough; if you sync across devices, it is cheap and polished.

alternatives.name: Apple Notes
alternatives.note: Free with iCloud sync across Apple devices.

alternatives.name: Obsidian
alternatives.note: Free for personal use; sync your vault with iCloud Drive at no extra cost.

cancel.howTo: Bear Pro is billed by Apple. iPhone: Settings, your name, Subscriptions, Bear, Cancel Subscription. Mac: App Store, your name, Account Settings, Subscriptions. Export notes you want to keep before you lose Pro sync.
cancel.gotchas: Pro includes iCloud sync, locked notes, and advanced exports (PDF, HTML, DOCX, JPG). Export anything you need first. Existing customers on the older $1.49 monthly or $14.99 yearly price keep it only while subscribed, so do not cancel and resubscribe.

name: Bitly (Core)
why: Core is $120 a year for 100 links a month. A short-link redirect service on a Cloudflare Worker with your own domain is a few hours of work and costs only the domain. Free allows 5 links a month.

alternatives.name: Bitly Free
alternatives.note: 5 links a month.

alternatives.name: Cloudflare Workers
alternatives.note: Free tier hosts a small redirect service.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A personal short-link service: create links with custom slugs behind a secret admin token, redirect quickly, count clicks by day and referrer, make QR codes, and export links as CSV.
rebuild.runsOn: Cloudflare Worker with KV or D1 on the free tier, on a domain you own (about $12 a year for a cheap TLD).
rebuild.youLose: Bitly's established link reputation with spam filters, branded-domain management, in-depth analytics, QR design tools, integrations and team features. If the Worker or domain lapses, every link you shared breaks.
rebuild.prompt: Build me a personal link shortener to replace Bitly Core, running on a Cloudflare Worker with D1 or KV on the free tier, on a domain I own. Features: a private admin page behind a long secret token where I create short links with optional custom slugs; fast 301 or 302 redirects; click counts per link by day with referrer and country, stored without IP addresses; QR code download for each link; link expiry; and CSV export of my links. My existing bit.ly links keep redirecting on Bitly, so only new links use my domain. Block redirects to private IP ranges and to non-http schemes. Write tests for slug generation and redirect rules. Provide Wrangler config, the commands to deploy and attach my domain, a warning about keeping the domain renewed, and a backup script that exports all links weekly.

cancel.howTo: In Bitly, open your account's Billing or Plan settings and cancel or downgrade to Free. Export your links and click data first.
cancel.gotchas: Core is annual-only ($120 a year), so a mid-year cancel is unlikely to refund the rest. After a downgrade, existing links keep redirecting but Free allows only 5 new links a month; check your branded-link and QR settings.

name: Calendly (Standard)
why: A booking page for one person is a small build: free hours from your calendar, a form, and a confirmation email. Calendly Free may already cover you; rebuild only if you need custom rules.

alternatives.name: Calendly Free
alternatives.note: The always-free plan handles basic one-on-one booking.

alternatives.name: Cal.com
alternatives.note: Open-source scheduling with a hosted free tier.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A booking page showing your open slots from Google Calendar, with meeting types, buffer times, timezone handling, and a Google Calendar invitation (with a Meet link) emailed to both of you, plus a private link to cancel or reschedule.
rebuild.runsOn: Static page on Cloudflare Pages plus a Cloudflare Worker (free tier) that reads Google Calendar free/busy and creates events through the Google Calendar API.
rebuild.youLose: Calendly's team routing, round-robin, polls, Zoom and Teams auto-links, SMS reminders, payment collection and polished mobile app. You also maintain the Google API credentials yourself, and the OAuth consent screen must be moved from Testing to In production or the token stops working after 7 days.
rebuild.prompt: Build me a personal booking page to replace Calendly Standard. First ask me for my current Calendly meeting types (name, length, buffer). Use a static front end (Vite, TypeScript) on Cloudflare Pages and a Cloudflare Worker for the API. Features: meeting types with duration and buffer, working-hours rules, minimum notice, visitor timezone detection, and available slots computed from my Google Calendar free/busy. A booking creates a Google Calendar event with a Meet link and sends the invitation to the visitor through Google (sendUpdates=all), so no email service is needed. Add a private manage link for cancelling or rescheduling. Use OAuth with my own Google Cloud project. Set the consent screen to In production (unverified is fine for one user), because refresh tokens issued in Testing expire after 7 days. Store the refresh token as a Worker secret, and add a /health check that reports invalid_grant. Add Cloudflare Turnstile spam protection. Write tests for slot generation across daylight-saving changes. Explain how to create the Google credentials and deploy on the free tier.

cancel.howTo: In Calendly, open Account settings, then Billing, and downgrade to Free or cancel. Check which event types and features revert to the free plan before you confirm.
cancel.gotchas: Standard is $10 per seat per month billed yearly; the page shows a 17 percent annual saving, so monthly billing costs more. Check for team seats you added before canceling.

name: Carrd Pro
why: Pro Standard is $19 a year for 10 sites with custom domains and forms. That is too little to beat with a weekend build, so keep it unless the sites are idle.

alternatives.name: Carrd Free
alternatives.note: Free plan for simple one-page sites on a carrd.co address.

alternatives.name: GitHub Pages
alternatives.note: Free static hosting if you are comfortable with files.

cancel.howTo: Open your Carrd dashboard, find the site's plan settings, and turn off auto-renewal or let the plan lapse. Download your site files first.
cancel.gotchas: Carrd plans can renew automatically each year or be paid as you go. Carrd's page does not say what happens to a custom domain, forms or embeds at expiry, so export first and test with a free account.

name: ClickUp
why: ClickUp is a team tool that holds shared work, so rebuilding it is off the table. Core is $9 per member on yearly billing ($12 regular price). For a solo user, Free Forever may be enough.

alternatives.name: ClickUp Free Forever
alternatives.note: Free plan for light personal use.

alternatives.name: Trello Free
alternatives.note: Simple boards at no cost.

cancel.howTo: As Workspace owner, open Workspace settings, then Billing, and downgrade to Free Forever or cancel. Remove guests and extra members first, since billing is per member.
cancel.gotchas: Prices are per member per month; the listed $9 is the yearly rate against a $12 regular price. Free Forever has usage limits, so check your storage and automations before you downgrade.

name: Craft Docs (Plus)
why: Craft Plus is $96 a year for unlimited documents and 30-day history. The free Starter plan holds 1,500 blocks, so keep Plus only if you outgrew that; Claude cannot replace its editor.

alternatives.name: Craft Starter (free)
alternatives.note: Free plan: 1,500 content blocks, 1 GB storage, 7-day history.

alternatives.name: Apple Notes
alternatives.note: Free and synced through iCloud.

cancel.howTo: Cancel in Craft's subscription settings, or in Apple or Google subscriptions if you subscribed in the app. Export documents (Markdown or PDF) before the plan lapses.
cancel.gotchas: Plus is $10 billed monthly or $96 billed yearly. Past the free limit of 1,500 blocks, new content may be restricted, so trim or export first.

name: Day One (Silver)
why: Silver is $49.99 a year for unlimited-device sync of an end-to-end encrypted journal. Journals are personal and long-lived, so a quick rebuild would risk your history. The free plan works on one device.

alternatives.name: Day One Basic (free)
alternatives.note: Unlimited text entries, one photo per entry, encryption, one device.

alternatives.name: Apple Notes
alternatives.note: Free, synced through iCloud, no end-to-end journaling features.

cancel.howTo: Cancel where you subscribed: Apple subscriptions on iPhone or Mac, Google Play on Android, or your Day One account for web purchases. Export your journals (JSON or PDF) first.
cancel.gotchas: Day One lists only yearly prices (Silver $49.99, Gold $74.99). Sync across devices is a paid feature, and the free plan covers one device, so export before downgrading to keep a full local copy.

name: DocuSign Personal
why: Personal is $120 billed yearly for 5 envelopes a month, which is easy to forget after one lease or loan. A legal e-signature trail is not something to rebuild; send with a free signer when you can.

alternatives.name: Adobe Acrobat Fill and Sign
alternatives.note: Free signing of your own PDFs.

alternatives.name: Dropbox Sign
alternatives.note: Has a free plan with a small monthly signature allowance.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to your DocuSign account, open the plan or billing page, and turn off auto-renew. If the web account shows no cancel option, contact DocuSign support to cancel before the renewal date.
cancel.gotchas: Personal is billed annually at $120 and limited to 5 envelopes a month, so a plan you used once still renews. Download completed documents before the plan ends.

name: Doodle (Pro)
why: Doodle's free plan runs basic group polls; Pro is a convenience for people who organize often. Most one-to-one scheduling is covered by Google Calendar or Calendly Free.

alternatives.name: Doodle Free
alternatives.note: Group polls without a paid plan.

alternatives.name: When2meet
alternatives.note: Free availability grid with no account needed.

cancel.howTo: Log in at doodle.com, open your profile menu, then Billing or Subscription, and turn off renewal or downgrade to Free. Close open polls first if you rely on paid options.
cancel.gotchas: Published prices conflict across sources (older pages show $6.95, newer ones about $11 a month on yearly billing), so read the amount on your own receipt. Annual plans renew automatically.

name: Evernote
why: Evernote's plans and prices have changed repeatedly and the free tier is capped at 50 notes. Joplin imports Evernote ENEX exports and syncs to a small box you own, with no per-month fee.

alternatives.name: Joplin
alternatives.note: Open-source notes app; imports ENEX files and syncs through Nextcloud, WebDAV, Dropbox, OneDrive or S3.

alternatives.name: Obsidian
alternatives.note: Free for personal use, local Markdown files; has an Evernote importer plugin.

selfhost.youLose: Evernote's polished web clipper, email-to-note, and attachment search. Sync only works while the server box is on, and you are the one who updates it and checks the backups.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. Set up Joplin as my Evernote replacement. Target: a Raspberry Pi 4 or an old laptop running Debian or Ubuntu Server. Install Docker, then run Nextcloud in a compose file with a named volume and a nightly backup job (rsync to a USB drive, keep 14 days). Install Tailscale on the server, my phone and my laptop so sync works away from home without opening router ports. Then walk me through installing Joplin on my desktop and phone, setting the sync target to Nextcloud, turning on Joplin's end-to-end encryption, and importing my Evernote export (ENEX files, one per notebook) with tags preserved. Finish with a one-page README covering updates, restoring from backup, and what to check if sync stalls. Ask me which operating system and phone I use before you start.

cancel.howTo: Export your notebooks first (select a notebook, then export as ENEX). Then cancel where you subscribed: your Evernote account's subscription settings on the web, or Apple or Google subscriptions if you bought in the app.
cancel.gotchas: Plan names and prices have changed repeatedly, so read your receipt for the plan and renewal date. The free plan is limited to 50 notes, 1 notebook and 1 device, so export before you downgrade.

name: Fantastical (Premium)
why: Fantastical is a polished Apple-first calendar. Its free tier handles a simple calendar; Premium at about $57 a year pays for natural-language entry and integrations. Keep it only if you use those daily.

alternatives.name: Fantastical Free
alternatives.note: Free tier with a simple calendar and your existing accounts.

alternatives.name: Apple Calendar
alternatives.note: Free and built in.

cancel.howTo: If you subscribed through the App Store, cancel in Apple subscriptions: Settings, your name, Subscriptions, Fantastical. If you subscribed on flexibits.com, manage it in your Flexibits account.
cancel.gotchas: App Store prices listed are $6.99 and $56.99 for Premium and $10.49 and $89.99 for Families, but the listing does not state which is monthly or yearly, so check your receipt. Flexibits sells on both its site and the App Store.

name: Freedom (Premium)
why: Freedom's free plan blocks apps and sites on unlimited devices; Premium adds scheduling and Locked Mode. Phone and desktop focus modes cover most of that. Pay month to month only for crunch periods.

alternatives.name: Freedom Free
alternatives.note: App, website and internet blocking with custom blocklists on unlimited devices.

alternatives.name: Cold Turkey
alternatives.note: Desktop blocker with a free tier.

rotate.pattern: Pay the $8.99 monthly plan only in the weeks you need Locked Mode (a deadline, an exam period), cancel afterward, and use the free plan and built-in focus modes the rest of the year. If you pay yearly, the annual rate is already lower, so rotate only if you pay month to month.

cancel.howTo: Log in at freedom.to, open your account's subscription page, and cancel the Premium plan. Your account drops to the free plan, which keeps blocking without scheduling or Locked Mode.
cancel.gotchas: Premium is $3.33 a month on yearly billing, $8.99 monthly, or a one-time $99.50 for Forever. A free 7-day trial is offered, so cancel before it ends. Scheduled sessions stop when Premium ends.

name: Goodnotes (Pro)
why: Pro is $35.99 a year; Free keeps 3 files, and Essential is $11.99. If you handwrite on an iPad daily, keep it. Watch for the separate $9.99 monthly AI Pass add-on, which many people never use.

alternatives.name: Goodnotes Free
alternatives.note: Free forever, up to 3 files, limited AI.

alternatives.name: Apple Notes
alternatives.note: Free, with Apple Pencil support and iCloud sync.

cancel.howTo: Most Goodnotes plans are billed by Apple. iPhone or iPad: Settings, your name, Subscriptions, Goodnotes, Cancel Subscription. Check for a separate AI Pass entry and cancel it too if you do not use it.
cancel.gotchas: Pro has no monthly price; the only monthly charge is the AI Pass add-on at $9.99. The App Store also lists a $28.99 one-time option. Export notebooks as PDF before downgrading, since Free keeps only 3 files.

name: IFTTT Pro
why: Pro is about $66 a year for 20,000 credits. Most applets are an API call plus a trigger, which Claude Code can script. Check whether Free (1,000 credits) or Starter ($25 a year) already covers you.

alternatives.name: IFTTT Free
alternatives.note: Free plan includes 1,000 credits a month.

alternatives.name: Home Assistant
alternatives.note: Open-source local automation for smart-home applets.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A folder of small scripts, one per applet (planned for about five applets), run on Cloudflare Workers Cron Triggers or a webhook Worker, with a config file, a dry-run flag and failure alerts.
rebuild.runsOn: Cloudflare Workers free tier (Cron Triggers for frequent checks, plus webhooks); GitHub Actions cron on a private repo only for daily or hourly jobs.
rebuild.youLose: IFTTT's catalog of ready-made service connections, instant phone and location triggers, and its smart-home integrations. Services without a public API cannot be reproduced.
rebuild.prompt: Replace my IFTTT Pro applets with scripts. Ask me to paste my applet list, then classify each one as a scheduled check, a webhook, or a smart-home action. For the first two kinds, write small Python scripts in an automations/ folder that call each service's API directly, with a config file and a dry-run flag, and run frequent checks as Cloudflare Workers Cron Triggers (free), use GitHub Actions cron in a private repo only for daily or hourly jobs, and use a local systemd timer if the task needs my home network. Plan for up to five applets; if I list more, tell me the extra hours. For smart-home applets, tell me whether the device has a local API or whether I need Home Assistant, and give a short plan. Keep secrets in GitHub secrets, add retries, send me a notification when a run fails, and write a README table that maps each applet to its replacement. List any applet that depends on a service with no public API.

cancel.howTo: Log in at ifttt.com, open your account's subscription settings, and downgrade to Free. On mobile subscriptions, cancel in the App Store or Google Play instead.
cancel.gotchas: The page lists annual billing at a 30 percent discount, so monthly billing costs more. After a downgrade, applets beyond the Free plan's credit allowance stop firing.

name: Instapaper Premium
why: Premium is $59.99 a year for full-text search, PDF reading and Kindle delivery. Wallabag does the same job on a box you own, but the polished apps and Kindle delivery are the draw, so keep it if you use them.

alternatives.name: Instapaper Free
alternatives.note: Free accounts have a monthly cap of 5 notes and no full-text search.

alternatives.name: Wallabag
alternatives.note: Open-source read-it-later you host yourself.

selfhost.youLose: Instapaper's Kindle delivery, polished mobile reading and text-to-speech voices. You run the server, apply updates, and back it up, and saving only works while it is reachable.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. Set up Wallabag as my Instapaper replacement. Target: a Raspberry Pi 4, NAS or old laptop running Debian or Ubuntu Server. Write a Docker Compose file for Wallabag with Postgres, named volumes, a restart policy, and secrets in an env file outside the repository. Install Tailscale on the server, my phone and my laptop so the web app and mobile app reach it privately, with no open router ports. Add a nightly database dump and a weekly copy of the data folder to a USB drive, keeping 14 days. Then walk me through exporting my Instapaper archive, importing it into Wallabag, installing the browser extension and the mobile app, and testing a save from my phone. Finish with a README for updates and restoring from backup. Ask what hardware I have before starting.

cancel.howTo: Log in to Instapaper, open Settings, then Subscription, and cancel. If you subscribed in the iOS app, cancel in Apple subscriptions instead.
cancel.gotchas: Premium is $5.99 monthly or $59.99 yearly. Free accounts are limited to 5 notes a month and have no full-text search, so export your articles first.

name: Jotform (Bronze)
why: The free Starter plan gives 5 forms and 100 submissions a month. Bronze at about $408 a year only makes sense with 25 forms or 1,000 submissions; otherwise Google Forms or the free tier covers it.

alternatives.name: Jotform Starter (free)
alternatives.note: 5 forms and 100 submissions a month.

alternatives.name: Google Forms
alternatives.note: Free with unlimited responses.

cancel.howTo: Log in to Jotform, open your account's Plan or Billing page, and downgrade to Starter. Forms beyond the free limit may be disabled, so archive or delete the ones you do not need first.
cancel.gotchas: Bronze is $34 a month billed yearly ($408) or $39 billed monthly. The Starter plan allows 5 active forms and 100 submissions a month, so anything above that can stop working after the downgrade.

name: Kit (ConvertKit)
why: Kit holds your subscriber list, so it is not a candidate for a rebuild. Its Free plan covers up to 10,000 subscribers, so keep Creator only for the sequences, automations or sales tools you actually use.

alternatives.name: Kit Free
alternatives.note: Free plan for up to 10,000 subscribers.

alternatives.name: Buttondown
alternatives.note: Low-cost newsletter tool for writers.

cancel.howTo: In Kit, open Account settings, then Billing, and cancel or downgrade to the Free plan. Export your subscribers as CSV first.
cancel.gotchas: When you pass your plan's subscriber limit, Kit automatically moves you to the next tier. The discounted first-year Pro price renews at the standard rate. Creator is about $390 billed yearly, saving $78 versus monthly.

name: Linktree Pro
why: A link-in-bio page is a static page with click counting, about four hours of work. Pro runs about $144 a year; the free plan covers a basic page if you do not need analytics.

alternatives.name: Linktree Free
alternatives.note: A basic link page at no cost.

alternatives.name: Carrd
alternatives.note: One-page sites; the Pro Standard plan is $19 a year.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A static link-in-bio page from a links.json file, with themes, social icons, a QR code, and private per-link click stats counted by a tiny Worker.
rebuild.runsOn: Cloudflare Pages (free) with a Cloudflare Worker and D1 on the free tier for click counts. Your own domain is optional.
rebuild.youLose: Linktree's drag-and-drop editor, scheduling, email and payment blocks, social-platform integrations and audience analytics. Link updates mean editing a JSON file.
rebuild.prompt: First ask me to paste my current links (title and URL). Then build me a link-in-bio page to replace Linktree Pro. A single static page (plain HTML, CSS and a little TypeScript, no framework) generated from one links.json file: avatar, name, short bio, a list of link buttons with optional icons, a social icon row, light and dark themes that follow the system, Open Graph tags, and fast load with no third-party scripts. Add click counting: each button goes through a /go/<id> route handled by a Cloudflare Worker that logs the click to a D1 table and then redirects, plus a private /stats page protected by a token that shows clicks per link by day. Include a QR code generated at build time. Deploy on Cloudflare Pages free tier, show how to attach my own domain, and give me a one-command way to update links.

cancel.howTo: In Linktree, open Settings, then Billing or Subscription, and cancel or downgrade to Free. Export your link list before the plan ends.
cancel.gotchas: Pro is roughly $15 billed monthly or $12 a month billed yearly; the yearly bill is charged upfront. Pro-only themes and analytics revert when you downgrade.

name: Loom (Business)
why: Loom Business is $18 a month per creator. A screen recorder with a private share link is a one-person tool Claude Code can build. The free Starter plan allows 25 videos of 5 minutes each.

alternatives.name: Loom Starter (free)
alternatives.note: 25 videos, 5-minute recordings, 720p.

alternatives.name: OBS Studio
alternatives.note: Free open-source screen and camera recorder for local files.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A browser screen recorder with optional camera bubble and mic, saved locally or uploaded to cloud storage, with an unguessable share link and a simple viewer page. No trimming or editing.
rebuild.runsOn: Static PWA on Cloudflare Pages, uploads to Cloudflare R2 (free allowance; R2 needs a payment method on file), small Worker for share links. Recording uses the browser's screen-capture and MediaRecorder APIs.
rebuild.youLose: Loom's instant desktop app, viewer comments and reactions, view analytics, auto transcripts and AI summaries, and workspace sharing. Browser recording is limited on some phones and tabs, and the R2 free tier has storage caps. Older Safari may not play WebM, so MP4 is preferred wherever the browser can record it.
rebuild.prompt: Build me a screen recording tool to replace Loom Business. A static PWA (Vite, TypeScript) that records my screen with optional webcam bubble and microphone using getDisplayMedia and MediaRecorder, shows a countdown, and has pause and stop controls. Save the recording locally, or upload it straight to Cloudflare R2 through a presigned URL from a Cloudflare Worker, and return a share link with a long random id. Prefer MP4 H.264 when MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported allows it, fall back to WebM, and tell me which format each recording uses. The share page plays the video with a minimal player, no tracking, and an optional expiry date. Add a library page listing my recordings with delete. Keep the Worker secret in environment variables. Deploy on Cloudflare Pages free tier and tell me the R2 storage and request limits I should watch. Do not add trimming in the first version. Include a README for setup.

cancel.howTo: Workspace admin: open Loom's Settings, then Billing, and cancel the plan or downgrade to Starter. Download the videos you want to keep first.
cancel.gotchas: Annual billing saves up to 17 percent, and a deactivated member's seat fees are forfeited for the rest of the billing cycle. On Starter, videos beyond the 25-video limit may become unavailable, so download them first.

name: Mailchimp
why: Mailchimp prices by contact count and holds your subscriber list, so a rebuild is off the table. Prune dead contacts, then ask for a retention rate. Its Free plan stops at 250 contacts.

alternatives.name: Kit Free
alternatives.note: Free plan for up to 10,000 subscribers.

alternatives.name: Mailchimp Free
alternatives.note: Free plan limited to 250 contacts.

haggle.leverage: Competing free and low-cost newsletter tools: Kit's Free plan covers up to 10,000 subscribers, while Mailchimp's Free plan stops at 250 contacts. Cleaning inactive contacts also lowers the tier.
haggle.script: Hi, I have been a Mailchimp customer for a while and I am reviewing my email tools. Kit offers a free plan for up to 10,000 subscribers, so I am planning to move my list unless I can get a better rate. I have already removed inactive contacts. Is there a retention discount, a longer-term rate, or a lower plan that fits my list size? If you can keep me under my current monthly price, I would rather stay.
haggle.bestTime: A week or two before renewal, after you clean inactive contacts. Contact support, or start the downgrade flow and see whether a retention offer appears.

cancel.howTo: Export your audience and campaign reports first. To downgrade, click your profile icon, choose Account, open Billing, then Monthly plans or credits, click Change Plan under Marketing Plan and pick Free. To close the account entirely, follow the Pause or Cancel Your Account help article.
cancel.gotchas: A paid plan can be downgraded to Free only once over the life of the account, and the downgrade takes effect when the next billing cycle begins. Your bill follows the number of contacts you hold, so archive or delete contacts you no longer email before renewing.

name: Make (Integromat)
why: Make Core is about $9 a month for 10,000 credits. Each scenario is a trigger plus a few API calls, which Claude Code can write as scheduled Worker scripts. Free gives 1,000 credits a month.

alternatives.name: Make Free
alternatives.note: Free plan includes 1,000 credits a month.

alternatives.name: Activepieces
alternatives.note: MIT-licensed open-source automation you can self-host.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A TypeScript project for Cloudflare Workers with one module per scenario (planned for about five scenarios), using Cron Triggers or webhooks, KV for de-duplication, retries and failure alerts.
rebuild.runsOn: Cloudflare Workers free tier (Cron Triggers, KV), deployed with Wrangler.
rebuild.youLose: Make's visual scenario builder, hundreds of ready-made modules, execution history with replay, and data-store tooling. Workers' free tier has request and CPU limits that heavy scenarios can exceed.
rebuild.prompt: Replace my Make scenarios with code. Plan for up to five scenarios; if I list more, tell me the extra hours. Ask me to describe each scenario's trigger, modules and filters, or paste the exported blueprint JSON. Then build a TypeScript project for Cloudflare Workers with one module per scenario, each exposing a scheduled handler (Cron Triggers) or an HTTP webhook handler, shared helpers for fetch with retries, and typed config. Use KV to remember what has already been processed so nothing runs twice. Keep API keys as Worker secrets. Add a dry-run mode, structured logs, and an email or webhook alert when a run fails. Include a test file per scenario using recorded sample payloads. Finish with a README that maps each scenario to its script and lists the steps to run both in parallel for a week before I cancel Make.

cancel.howTo: In Make, open your organization's Billing settings and cancel the subscription or switch to the Free plan. Deactivate scenarios you no longer need first.
cancel.gotchas: Annual plans are cheaper than monthly but bill upfront, so check your renewal date before canceling. The Free plan allows 1,000 credits a month, and scenarios that need more will stop once you use them up.

name: Notion (Plus)
why: A solo workspace often fits the Free plan. Plus mainly adds bigger uploads and longer page history. Nothing Claude builds in a weekend replaces Notion's databases, so keep it if you use them.

alternatives.name: Notion Free plan
alternatives.note: Same app, no cost. Check your file sizes and history needs first.

alternatives.name: Obsidian
alternatives.note: Free for personal use; notes are plain Markdown files on your devices.

cancel.howTo: Workspace owner only: open Settings in the sidebar, then Billing, then Change plan, choose Free and confirm. The downgrade takes effect at the end of the billing cycle, and the confirmation shows the end date.
cancel.gotchas: Only workspace owners can see or change plans. Removing members lowers the bill at the next cycle, not mid-cycle. Notion refunds in full if you downgrade within 3 days of signing up for monthly billing or 30 days for annual; later than that, expect no refund.

name: Obsidian Sync
why: Obsidian is free; Sync is $48 a year for hassle-free phone and laptop sync. Syncthing can replace it between computers and Android, but iPhone has no official Syncthing app, so keep Sync if you use an iPhone.

alternatives.name: iCloud Drive vault
alternatives.note: Free for Apple-only users: keep the vault in iCloud Drive.

alternatives.name: Syncthing
alternatives.note: Open-source file sync between your own computers, no cloud server.

software: Tailscale (free tier) for remote access to the hub
selfhost.youLose: Obsidian Sync's one-click setup, version history and iPhone support. Syncthing has no official iOS app, so an iPhone needs iCloud Drive or a paid third-party Syncthing client instead.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. Replace Obsidian Sync with Syncthing. My always-on hub is a Raspberry Pi or old laptop running Debian or Ubuntu. Install Syncthing as a systemd service on the hub, keep its GUI bound to localhost, and reach it over Tailscale. Create a shared folder for my Obsidian vault with the hub set as an introducer and file versioning set to staggered. Pair it with my laptop and desktop, and set ignore patterns for the .obsidian/workspace files and the .trash folder so settings do not fight. Add a weekly encrypted backup of the vault from the hub to a USB drive. Explain how to handle sync conflicts in Markdown files, and tell me plainly what I should do on my iPhone instead (for example iCloud Drive). Ask what devices I own before you begin.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to your Obsidian account on obsidian.md and cancel the Sync subscription there. Your vault stays on every device where it is already synced; the remote copy and version history belong to the subscription.
cancel.gotchas: Sync Standard is $4 a month billed yearly or $5 billed monthly; Plus is $8 or $10. Confirm every device has the full vault locally before canceling, because the remote history will not be there afterward.

name: Raindrop.io Pro
why: Raindrop Free keeps unlimited bookmarks and devices; Pro adds full-text search, permanent copies and backups. Keep it if you use those. If not, downgrade, or run linkding on a Pi.

alternatives.name: Raindrop.io Free
alternatives.note: Free plan keeps unlimited bookmarks, collections and devices.

alternatives.name: linkding
alternatives.note: Self-hosted bookmark manager, one Docker container with SQLite.

software: Browser extension for Firefox or Chrome
selfhost.youLose: Raindrop's polished mobile apps and visual boards, nested collections, sharing, and one-click permanent copies. linkding is deliberately minimal, and you handle updates and backups.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. Set up linkding as my Raindrop.io Pro replacement. Target: a Raspberry Pi, NAS or old laptop running Debian or Ubuntu Server. Write a Docker Compose file for linkding with a named volume, a restart policy, and the admin password set through an env file kept out of the repository. Install Tailscale on the server, my laptop and my phone so I reach it privately with no open router ports. Add a nightly backup of the SQLite database and data folder to a USB drive, keeping 14 days, and a restore test. Then walk me through exporting my Raindrop bookmarks as HTML, writing a small script that turns each collection into a tag, importing the file into linkding, installing the browser extension, and adding a phone bookmarklet or share shortcut. End with a short README for updates. Ask what hardware I have before starting.

cancel.howTo: Log in at raindrop.io, open Settings, then Pro, and cancel the subscription. Export your bookmarks (HTML or CSV) first so they stay available on the free plan or elsewhere.
cancel.gotchas: Yearly billing is usually about 20 percent cheaper than monthly. Raindrop's page did not show dollar prices when checked, so read your receipt. Permanent copies and full-text search are Pro features and stop with the plan.

name: Readwise
why: If you mainly want highlights resurfaced, a daily-review app with Kindle import is a weekend build. If you read in Reader, keep it. Highlights Lite is $5.59 a month if you only want daily review.

alternatives.name: Readwise Highlights Lite
alternatives.note: $5.59 a month on yearly billing: daily review, search and sync.

alternatives.name: Obsidian
alternatives.note: Keep highlights as Markdown notes in a free local vault.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A highlight vault that imports Kindle clippings and Readwise CSV exports, with tags, notes, search, a daily review of a handful of highlights, and Markdown export.
rebuild.runsOn: Installable PWA on Cloudflare Pages (free) with highlights in IndexedDB. The daily review lives in the app.
rebuild.youLose: Reader (read-it-later, RSS, PDF and EPUB highlighting), automatic syncing from Kindle and other services, and Readwise's tuned review scheduler. You would re-import highlights by file.
rebuild.prompt: Build me a highlight vault to replace Readwise Highlights. An installable PWA (Vite, React, TypeScript) storing everything in IndexedDB. Import: Kindle My Clippings.txt (parse book, author, location, note vs highlight), a Readwise CSV export, and plain Markdown. Features: books and sources list, tags, my own notes on each highlight, full-text search, favorite and discard buttons, and a Daily Review page that shows five highlights chosen by weighting older and favorited ones, with Remembered and Skip buttons that feed a simple spaced-repetition schedule. Add Markdown export (one file per book) and JSON backup and restore. Write tests for the clippings parser using sample files. Deploy to Cloudflare Pages free tier, explain installing it on a phone, and note what to do about duplicate highlights on re-import.

cancel.howTo: Log in at readwise.io, open Account settings, then Billing, and cancel the subscription. Export your highlights (CSV or Markdown) first.
cancel.gotchas: Prices are quoted for yearly billing and the yearly plan saves up to 23 percent versus monthly. The trial lasts 30 days, so cancel before it ends if you are not continuing.

name: RescueTime
why: Solo Focus is $9 a month or $84 a year. Check how often you open the reports. ActivityWatch tracks apps and sites for free with data on your own device; Screen Time covers phones.

alternatives.name: ActivityWatch
alternatives.note: Open-source app and web tracking for Windows, macOS, Linux and Android; data stays local.

alternatives.name: RescueTime Lite
alternatives.note: Premium falls back to the free Lite plan after you cancel.

cancel.howTo: Log in at rescuetime.com, open Account Settings, then Billing, click Cancel my subscription on the right, and follow the prompts. Paid features stay available until the current billing cycle ends, then the account reverts to the free Lite plan.
cancel.gotchas: Paid plans have a 14-day free trial and you are not charged if you cancel before it ends, but prorated refunds for partial periods are generally not offered. Remove the desktop app after canceling.

name: Roam Research
why: Roam has no free tier and costs $165 a year, while Logseq (open source, local files) covers daily notes and backlinks at no cost. Moving takes an afternoon and your notes become plain files.

alternatives.name: Logseq
alternatives.note: Open-source, local-first outliner with backlinks and daily notes.

alternatives.name: Obsidian
alternatives.note: Free for personal use; local Markdown vault with backlinks.

software: Tailscale (free tier) for remote access to the hub
selfhost.youLose: Roam's hosted multiplayer graph, its polished web app, and any extensions you rely on. Roam-specific block references may need cleanup after import, and iPhone sync needs an extra route since Syncthing has no iOS app.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. Migrate me from Roam Research to Logseq. First, tell me how to export my Roam graph (JSON and Markdown) and keep a copy. Then help me install Logseq on my computers, import the export, and check daily notes, page links, tags and block references. List what did not convert and write a small script that reports broken references. For sync, set up Syncthing between my machines with an always-on hub (Raspberry Pi or old laptop on Debian or Ubuntu), keep the Syncthing GUI on localhost, reach the hub over Tailscale, and schedule a weekly backup of the graph folder to a USB drive. Add a short guide on how my daily-notes habit maps to Logseq's journals. Ask which operating systems I use first.

cancel.howTo: Export your graph first (the graph menu, Export All, JSON and Markdown). Then cancel the subscription in Roam's account or billing settings before the next renewal.
cancel.gotchas: Roam has no free tier, so access ends with the plan. Pro is $15 billed monthly or about $165 billed yearly, and there is a five-year Believer plan, so check which one you are on before canceling.

name: SaneBox
why: SaneBox sorts mail by sender into a lesser-priority folder. A script on your own computer can learn the same thing from your read and reply history. Gmail and Outlook filters cover the basics for free.

alternatives.name: Gmail filters and tabs
alternatives.note: Built-in filters to label and skip the inbox.

alternatives.name: Spark Mail Free
alternatives.note: Free plan with smart inbox sorting.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A script that reads your mailbox over IMAP, scores each sender by how often you open and reply, moves low-score senders to a Later folder, and keeps a Digest note of what it moved.
rebuild.runsOn: Python script on your own computer or an old laptop on a schedule, using a Gmail app password, or OAuth2 (XOAUTH2) for Outlook.com and Microsoft 365, with read and move permissions only. Free.
rebuild.youLose: SaneBox's trained filtering across providers, reminders and snooze folders, one-click training from any mail app, and support. The script touches your mailbox credentials, so keep it local and read-only until you trust it. Microsoft no longer accepts app passwords for IMAP, so Outlook needs your own Entra app registration and an OAuth2 sign-in.
rebuild.prompt: Build me a local email triage script to replace SaneBox. Python 3, running on my own computer on a schedule. Connect over IMAP with a Gmail app password (2-step verification required) stored in the OS keychain, or for Outlook.com and Microsoft 365 with OAuth2 and XOAUTH2 through my own Entra app registration (MSAL device-code flow, token cache in the keychain), because Microsoft no longer accepts app passwords for IMAP. Start in dry-run mode that only prints what it would move. Score each sender from my last 90 days (share of messages I opened, replied to, or starred). Move low-score senders into a folder called Later and keep a Digest note listing what moved. Never touch flagged, starred or unread messages from anyone I have replied to. Let me rescue a sender by dragging a message back, which the script learns from. Log every move to a CSV with an undo command. Add unit tests for the scoring and a README with setup for Gmail and Outlook and how to schedule it.

cancel.howTo: Log in at sanebox.com, open your account's subscription settings, and cancel. Messages SaneBox moved into its folders stay in your mailbox, so move anything you want back to the inbox first.
cancel.gotchas: SaneBox's current prices were not visible on its pricing page, so check your receipt for the plan and renewal date. Disconnect SaneBox's access to your mail account after canceling.

name: Smallpdf Pro
why: Smallpdf is a web toolbox for merging, compressing and signing PDFs. Free use is enough for occasional jobs, and Stirling-PDF or your OS's built-in tools do the same offline. Confirm renewal terms on your receipt.

alternatives.name: Stirling-PDF
alternatives.note: Open-core PDF toolkit you run yourself; 50+ tools, runs in Docker or as a desktop app.

alternatives.name: macOS Preview
alternatives.note: Built in on Mac: merge, sign and annotate PDFs.

selfhost.youLose: Smallpdf's polished web flow and cloud-drive hookups. Stirling-PDF is open-core, so enterprise features are paid, and you handle updates. Its desktop app needs no server at all if you only work on one computer.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. Set up Stirling-PDF as my Smallpdf replacement. Target: an old laptop or NAS running Debian or Ubuntu Server (or tell me to use the desktop app if I only work on one computer). Write a Docker Compose file that runs the Stirling-PDF container on port 8080 with a restart policy, a volume for configuration, and login enabled so only I can use it. Install Tailscale on the server and my devices so I can open it from my laptop and phone without exposing it to the internet. Walk me through the five operations I use most: merge, split, compress, rotate, and sign. Add a note on keeping the image updated and one on backing up its settings. Ask what devices I own before you begin.

cancel.howTo: Log in to Smallpdf, open Account settings, then Subscription or Billing, and cancel the plan. Cancel before any trial period ends so it does not convert to a paid plan.
cancel.gotchas: Smallpdf's current prices were not visible on its pricing page, so check your receipt for the plan, billing period and renewal date. Annual plans bill upfront.

name: Spark Mail (Plus)
why: Spark's pricing page now lists Free, Plus ($99 a year) and Pro ($199). Free runs mail fine; Plus adds AI features, and Claude can draft replies if you paste a thread. Keep Plus only for what Free lacks.

alternatives.name: Spark Free
alternatives.note: Free plan for personal mail.

alternatives.name: Apple Mail
alternatives.note: Free and built in on Apple devices.

cancel.howTo: If you subscribed in the app on iPhone or Mac, cancel in Apple subscriptions; on Android, in Google Play. For web or Stripe purchases, use Spark's account settings.
