cancel.gotchas: Plus is $10 monthly or $99 yearly, Pro $20 monthly or $199 yearly. Annual plans bill upfront, so cancel at least a day before renewal. If you started on a free trial, cancel before it ends.

name: Superhuman
why: A fast email client is a speed tool you either value or you do not, and Claude cannot replace the inbox. Superhuman also sells Grammarly and suite plans (Pro $12 a month yearly), so check which product you pay for.

alternatives.name: Gmail keyboard shortcuts
alternatives.note: Free; turn them on in Gmail settings.

alternatives.name: Spark Mail Free
alternatives.note: Free plan with a fast inbox on every platform.

cancel.howTo: Open Superhuman settings or your account's billing page and cancel the plan there. If you pay through an employer or an app store, cancel through that channel instead.
cancel.gotchas: Superhuman's plans page lists Free, Pro ($12 yearly, $15 monthly) and Business ($33 yearly, $40 monthly), with Mail features under Business, and it also sells Grammarly, so a charge may be for another product. The standalone Mail price could not be confirmed from the site.

name: SurveyMonkey
why: Individual plans run $468 a year or $149 a month, and many people need only one survey. Google Forms or the free Basic plan (10 questions) handles occasional surveys. Cancel before auto-renew.

alternatives.name: Google Forms
alternatives.note: Free, unlimited questions and responses.

alternatives.name: SurveyMonkey Basic (free)
alternatives.note: One user, 10 questions per survey, limited responses.

cancel.howTo: Sign in, open your account's Billing details, and turn off auto-renew. At the end of the billing cycle the account moves to the free Basic plan.
cancel.gotchas: Auto-renew is on by default. Responses beyond your plan limit are charged at $0.15 each. The monthly Standard plan is $149 a month, so a forgotten month-to-month plan is expensive. Export your results first.

name: TickTick Premium
why: Premium unlocks higher limits and extra views on top of a capable free plan. Cheap enough to keep if you hit those limits, easy to drop to Free if you only keep simple lists.

alternatives.name: TickTick Free
alternatives.note: Lists, due dates and reminders stay free; Premium unlocks the extra views and limits.

alternatives.name: Todoist Beginner (free)
alternatives.note: Free plan keeps your tasks with tighter project limits.

cancel.howTo: Cancel where you bought it. App Store: Settings, your name, Subscriptions, TickTick, Cancel Subscription. Google Play: Payments and subscriptions, Subscriptions, TickTick, Cancel. Web purchases: manage the plan in TickTick account settings.
cancel.gotchas: Deleting the app does not cancel the subscription. The App Store price ($4.99 monthly, $49.99 yearly) can be higher than the price on TickTick's own site, so check which channel you used.

name: Todoist Pro
why: A personal task list is a weekend of work for Claude Code, and Pro now costs $60 a year. The catch is reliable phone reminders and sync, so rebuild only if you can live with PWA limits.

alternatives.name: Todoist Beginner (free)
alternatives.note: Free plan keeps your tasks but limits active projects to 5.

alternatives.name: TickTick free plan
alternatives.note: Free tier covers lists, due dates and a basic calendar.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A task app with inbox, projects, sections, natural-language due dates ("every Monday"), priorities, labels, Today and Upcoming views, in-app reminders, a private .ics calendar feed, and optional cross-device sync through a free Cloudflare Worker.
rebuild.runsOn: Installable PWA on Cloudflare Pages (free tier), data in IndexedDB, optional sync via a Cloudflare Worker with D1 or KV (free tier).
rebuild.youLose: Todoist's mature natural-language parser, shared projects, true push reminders on iPhone (a PWA cannot alert you while closed; the calendar feed is the workaround), email-to-task, calendar integrations, and support when something breaks.
rebuild.prompt: Build me a personal task manager to replace Todoist Pro, as an installable PWA using Vite, React and TypeScript. Core features: inbox, projects with sections, due dates entered in plain language such as "every Monday" or "tomorrow 5pm", priorities, labels, and Today and Upcoming views. Store everything in IndexedDB. For phone-to-laptop sync, add a small Cloudflare Worker with a D1 or KV store behind one secret token that I set, using last-write-wins per task. Show in-app reminders while the app is open, and serve a private .ics feed from the Worker so my calendar app sends the real notifications. Import my Todoist CSV exports (one file per project; columns TYPE, CONTENT, DESCRIPTION, PRIORITY, INDENT, DATE; sections are TYPE=section) and tell me labels and comments are not in the CSV. Export everything to JSON. Write unit tests for the date parser and the sync merge. Deploy the PWA to Cloudflare Pages on the free tier and explain how I install it on iPhone and Android. Keep it under 3,000 lines and write a README with setup steps.

cancel.howTo: On the web or desktop app: click your avatar, open Settings, then Subscription, choose Cancel plan and confirm. If you subscribed through the App Store or Google Play, cancel there instead.
cancel.gotchas: Pro stays active until the period ends, then the account drops to the free plan: active personal projects go from 300 to 5 and automatic backups stop. Yearly web purchases can be refunded within 30 days.

name: Toggl Track (Starter)
why: Toggl's Free plan covers timers, calendar integrations and basic planning. Starter ($9 yearly, $12 monthly) adds billable rates, timeline views and team reports. Downgrade unless you invoice from it.

alternatives.name: Toggl Track Free
alternatives.note: Manual and live timers, calendar integrations, basic planning.

alternatives.name: ActivityWatch
alternatives.note: Open-source automatic app and web tracking, data stays on your device.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A personal time tracker with start and stop timers, projects, tags, manual entries, weekly and monthly reports, billable rates, and CSV export for invoices.
rebuild.runsOn: Installable PWA on Cloudflare Pages (free) with data in IndexedDB.
rebuild.youLose: Toggl's team features, browser and desktop timers, integrations, reminders and idle detection. Without a sync server, your phone and laptop keep separate data unless you move the backup file between them.
rebuild.prompt: Build me a personal time tracker to replace Toggl Track. An installable PWA (Vite, React, TypeScript) with data in IndexedDB. Features: a one-tap start and stop timer with description, project and tags; manual entries and editing; projects with a hourly rate and client name; a weekly timesheet view; reports by day, week, project and tag with simple bar charts; CSV export for invoices; and JSON backup and restore. Add a Pomodoro-style reminder using the Notifications API that I can switch off. Import my Toggl detailed-report CSV (columns User, Email, Client, Project, Task, Description, Billable, Start date, Start time, End date, End time, Duration, Tags). Write tests for duration rounding and the report totals across time zones and daylight saving. Deploy to Cloudflare Pages free tier, explain how to install it on a phone and laptop, and say how to move data between them.

cancel.howTo: In Toggl Track, open Organization or Profile settings, then Subscription, and downgrade to the Free plan. Export your time entries as CSV from Reports first.
cancel.gotchas: Starter is $9 per user on yearly billing and $12 monthly. Free limits include no billable rates, timeline views or team-level reports, so check your invoices before you drop it.

name: Trello Premium
why: Premium adds Calendar, Timeline, Dashboard and Map views. Free allows 10 boards per Workspace and Standard ($5) removes the board cap. Downgrade unless you use those views daily.

alternatives.name: Trello Free
alternatives.note: Up to 10 boards per Workspace, unlimited cards.

alternatives.name: Trello Standard
alternatives.note: $5 per user per month on yearly billing; unlimited boards.

cancel.howTo: As Workspace admin, open Billing from the Workspace menu and downgrade to Standard or Free. Check that boards using Premium views still make sense afterward.
cancel.gotchas: Premium is $10 per user billed yearly or $12.50 monthly. Workspaces over 10 boards will be restricted on Free. Annual plans bill upfront, so downgrade before renewal.

name: Typeform (Basic)
why: Basic caps you at 100 responses a month on one seat. A one-question-at-a-time form that writes to a Google Sheet is a small build, and Google Forms is free if style does not matter.

alternatives.name: Google Forms
alternatives.note: Free, unlimited responses, writes to Google Sheets.

alternatives.name: Tally
alternatives.note: Free form builder with a one-question style.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A form renderer that shows one question at a time from a JSON definition, with conditional logic, progress bar, themes, spam protection and responses saved to a Google Sheet.
rebuild.runsOn: Static site on Cloudflare Pages (free) plus a Cloudflare Worker that writes to the Google Sheets API.
rebuild.youLose: Typeform's visual editor, analytics, integrations, hosted file uploads, payments and team features. Every new form means editing JSON or asking Claude for a change.
rebuild.prompt: First ask me to paste my questions or the form JSON from the Typeform API. Then build a personal form builder to replace Typeform Basic. Output: a static site (Vite, TypeScript) where I define a form in a JSON file and it renders one question at a time with keyboard navigation, a progress bar, conditional logic, required fields, and question types: short text, long text, multiple choice, rating, email and date. On submit, post to a Cloudflare Worker that appends the response to a Google Sheet through the Sheets API and sends me a notification email through Resend's free tier. Add spam protection with Cloudflare Turnstile, a light and dark theme, and CSV export from the sheet. Provide three sample forms (contact, feedback, RSVP). Deploy on Cloudflare Pages free tier and show how to share a form by link or iframe. Write the steps to create the Google service account and the Resend key.

cancel.howTo: In Typeform, open Account settings, then Billing or Plan, and choose Cancel subscription or Downgrade to Free. Export response data to CSV first.
cancel.gotchas: Typeform's own pricing page shows two sets of Basic prices (about $28 or $25 a month on yearly billing, $39 or $29 monthly), so read your receipt. Annual plans bill upfront.

name: Zapier
why: Most personal Zaps are an API call on a schedule or a webhook. Claude Code can turn them into scripts that run free on Cloudflare Workers or GitHub Actions. Zapier Free (100 tasks) may already cover a light user.

alternatives.name: Zapier Free
alternatives.note: Free plan includes 100 tasks a month.

alternatives.name: Activepieces
alternatives.note: MIT-licensed open-source automation you can self-host.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A repo of small TypeScript or Python scripts, one per Zap (planned for about five automations), run by Cloudflare Workers Cron Triggers and webhooks, with GitHub Actions for daily jobs, plus retries, logs and failure alerts.
rebuild.runsOn: Cloudflare Workers free tier (Cron Triggers for frequent polling, plus webhooks); GitHub Actions cron on a private repo (about 2,000 free minutes a month) only for daily or hourly jobs.
rebuild.youLose: Zapier's thousands of ready-made app connectors, the visual editor, replay of failed runs, and instant triggers. Apps without a usable public API cannot be automated this way, and you maintain every token yourself.
rebuild.prompt: Replace my Zapier Professional plan with scripts. First ask me to list my active Zaps and the apps each one touches, then group them into triggers (webhook, schedule, new email, new row) and actions. Plan for up to five automations; if I list more, tell me the extra hours. For each Zap, write a small TypeScript or Python script in an automations/ folder with typed config, retries, logging and a dry-run flag. Run polling jobs more often than hourly as Cloudflare Workers Cron Triggers (free). Use GitHub Actions cron in a private repo only for daily or hourly jobs, and tell me how many free minutes I am using. Receive webhooks with a free Worker. Store API keys as secrets, never in code. Add one job that sends me a failure summary by email or Slack webhook. Write a README mapping every old Zap to its new script, with a checklist for running both side by side for a week before I cancel. Flag any Zap that needs an app with no usable API.

software: Docker Compose with Postgres and Redis
selfhost.youLose: Zapier's hosted reliability: if the box is off or your home internet drops, automations stop. Activepieces has fewer ready-made connectors than Zapier, its enterprise features need a paid license, and you handle updates and backups.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. Set up Activepieces Community Edition on my spare machine to replace Zapier. Target: an old laptop or a NAS with Docker, with at least 2 CPU cores and 4 GB of RAM, running Debian or Ubuntu Server. Install Docker with Compose v2, then run the official install script from a dedicated folder so it starts the app, worker, Postgres and Redis containers. Back up the generated .env file, because stored connections cannot be decrypted without AP_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Put Tailscale on the box so I open the editor privately, and use a Cloudflare Tunnel only for webhook URLs that need public access. Add a nightly Postgres dump to a USB drive, keeping 14 days. Then help me recreate my three busiest Zaps as flows, test them, and write a short recovery note for what to do after a power cut. Ask which apps my Zaps use before starting.

cancel.howTo: Log in to Zapier, open Billing and usage, click Manage, and select the Free plan. Zapier has no separate Cancel button. Paid features continue until the end of the billing cycle.
cancel.gotchas: Zapier subscriptions are non-refundable. Pro tiers are priced by task volume, and annual billing is about a third lower than monthly ($19.99 against $29.99 at the lowest tier), so check which you are on. The Free plan allows 100 tasks a month; Zaps beyond that will not run.

name: Zoom Workplace Pro
why: Basic Zoom meetings are capped at 40 minutes and 100 people. Pro is $16.99 a month, or $14.16 on yearly billing. Pay month to month only in the months you host longer calls.

alternatives.name: Zoom Basic
alternatives.note: Free meetings up to 40 minutes and 100 participants.

alternatives.name: Google Meet
alternatives.note: Free video calls with a Google account; check the current time limit for group calls.

rotate.pattern: Stay on Basic and subscribe to the monthly Pro plan only in months when you host calls longer than 40 minutes, then cancel the same week. For occasional long calls, ask the other person to host or use another free meeting link.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at zoom.us, open Account Management, then Billing, and cancel the subscription or downgrade to Basic. Download cloud recordings first.
cancel.gotchas: Yearly billing is $14.16 a month charged upfront; monthly is $16.99. Cloud recordings and some settings are tied to Pro, so save what you need before the plan ends.

name: 23andMe Premium membership
why: Premium membership is $99/yr after a trial month, renews automatically and does not warn you before each charge. Save your reports and raw data, then cancel unless you want ongoing updates.

cancel.howTo: Go to your 23andMe Account Settings and cancel or modify your membership. To avoid the next charge, act at least one day before the next billing cycle.
cancel.gotchas: Free trials convert to paid automatically and the terms say you may not be notified before each charge. You keep access to the end of the paid period; afterwards you lose access to membership content, including genetic reports provided as part of the membership. Download the reports and raw data you want first. The company is now run as 23andMe Research Institute (23andme.org), and the older name 23andMe+ no longer appears on its pricing page.

name: Amazon Prime
why: Prime bundles delivery, video and perks for one fee, hard to beat if you order often. If you don't, the $14.99 monthly plan lets you pay only for the months you use it.

alternatives.name: Walmart+
alternatives.note: Cheaper at $98/yr with free delivery on grocery orders over its minimum; check it covers your usual stores.

rotate.pattern: Switch to the $14.99 monthly plan and hold Prime only for the months you really use it, such as November and December gifting, Prime Day or a move. The $139 annual plan only wins if you keep Prime more than about nine months a year.

cancel.howTo: On Amazon open Account & Lists > Prime Membership, choose Update, Cancel and More (menu labels shift), then End Membership and follow the prompts. If you joined through Google Play or another company, cancel there instead.
cancel.gotchas: The flow has several "keep my benefits" screens. A full refund generally needs cancelling within 3 business days of signing up, or no Prime benefits used since the last charge. Prime Video add-on channels such as Paramount+ are billed separately and may keep charging after Prime ends, so check Memberships & Subscriptions. Free Grubhub+ via Prime ends with it.

name: Ancestry
why: Record access is the product, and you can buy it in bursts. Subscribe for a research push, then cancel: your trees and DNA results stay on a free guest account.

alternatives.name: FamilySearch
alternatives.note: Free genealogy records and trees; many Ancestry users supplement or move their research here.

rotate.pattern: Buy a month or a few months when you plan a research push, download the records and sources you need, then cancel. Export your tree before you cancel so you keep a copy. Resubscribe when you have new leads.

cancel.howTo: Go to Account Settings, find the Membership section and select Cancel membership (or Cancel trial). Follow the prompts until you receive a confirmation number, and save it.
cancel.gotchas: Cancelling stops renewal but benefits continue to the expiration date. Charges can still occur if you cancel too close to renewal. Some semi-annual and annual memberships paid monthly carry a cancellation fee if you leave before the period ends. After expiry your account becomes a free Registered Guest account; trees and DNA results stay but with fewer features.

name: Apple News+
why: $12.99/mo for magazines, newspapers and puzzles, also bundled in Apple One Premier. Subscribe in months you read, cancel at least a day before renewal, and resubscribe later.

alternatives.name: Libby (your public library)
alternatives.note: Many libraries lend digital magazines and newspapers for free with a library card; availability varies by library.

alternatives.name: Apple News (free tier)
alternatives.note: The free app still covers headlines and free articles from many outlets.

rotate.pattern: Keep Apple News+ for a few months when you want magazines or the daily puzzles, then cancel. Apple restarts it any time from the News app. Check whether an Apple One Premier plan already bundles it before paying separately.

cancel.howTo: On iPhone open Settings, tap your name, then Subscriptions > Apple News+ > Cancel Subscription. You can also manage it from the Apple News app.
cancel.gotchas: Cancel at least a day before the renewal date. Cancelling during a free trial ends access immediately, including family members. If you have Apple News+ through Apple One Premier, you change the Apple One plan instead.

name: BarkBox
why: Monthly toy and treat box starting around $24 a month. Six- and twelve-month plans charge the remainder if you cancel early, so pick monthly or skip months.

rotate.pattern: Stay on the flexible monthly plan and skip months when the toy pile is already big. Skip a renewal or cancel before your next bill date from your account. Avoid 6 and 12 month prepay plans if you want to rotate.

cancel.howTo: Cancel or skip a renewal from your BarkBox account before your next bill date. To end a 6 or 12 month commitment early, contact the Happy Team.
cancel.gotchas: On 6 and 12 month plans the terms say you are charged for the rest of the commitment if you cancel early, and you must act by the first day of the month after your current subscription period ends. The homepage says "starting at $24 a month"; checkout shows the real price, and the price depends on plan length and add-ons.

name: Blue Apron
why: Weekly boxes bill automatically, with per-serving price falling as order size grows and a shipping fee on top. Skip weeks in advance and keep it for weeks you actually cook.

rotate.pattern: Skip upcoming deliveries up to five weeks ahead from the Upcoming page and keep a rolling plan of two or three boxes a month. There is no minimum commitment, so you can also pause for a few months. Savings are modest because you still buy groceries in skipped weeks.

cancel.howTo: Open Plan Settings, choose Edit, then Pause/Cancel Subscription and follow the prompts.
cancel.gotchas: Orders marked Order Processed or Shipped on the Upcoming page have already been charged and cannot be cancelled. The plan auto-renews, so skip or cancel before the weekly cutoff. Blue Apron+ (about $9.99/month per the company blog) is a separate paid membership for free shipping; check you did not enroll. Shipping and per-serving prices on the support page may be dated.

name: Bumble
why: Premium and Boost renew automatically at varying prices (the App Store lists several price points). Buy only while actively using the app and end auto-renew straight away.

rotate.pattern: Buy the shortest term only while you are actively using Bumble, switch auto-renew off the same day you buy, and let it lapse during breaks. Longer plans look cheaper per month but renew automatically for the full term.

cancel.howTo: Cancel where you bought it: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > Bumble; Android Google Play > Subscriptions; web purchases through the subscription settings in the Bumble app or the Bumble support site.
cancel.gotchas: Deleting the app or your account does not stop billing from Apple or Google. The App Store lists Premium at $17.99 to $32.99 and Boost at $2.99 to $12.99, and it does not say which plan length each price covers. BumbleCoins and one-off purchases are separate.

name: Costco membership
why: Annual fee of $65 (Gold Star) or $130 (Executive). Worth it only if your savings and Executive rewards exceed the fee; Costco says it refunds the fee any time you are dissatisfied, so lock-in risk is low.

cancel.howTo: Ask at a warehouse membership counter, call or chat with Member Services, or turn off auto-renewal in your Costco.com account. Do it before your renewal date.
cancel.gotchas: Auto-renewal charges the card around your renewal month, so turn it off ahead of time. Executive members earn a 2% Reward on the membership year, so ask Costco what you forfeit before you downgrade or cancel mid-year. Costco says it will cancel and refund the fee at any time if you are dissatisfied.

name: Discord Nitro
why: Nitro is $9.99/mo ($2.99 Basic): bigger uploads, custom emoji, HD streaming and profile perks. Keep it if you use them weekly; otherwise cancel and the free tier remains.

cancel.howTo: In Discord open User Settings > Subscriptions and cancel Nitro. If you subscribed through Apple or Google, cancel in those subscription settings instead.
cancel.gotchas: Server Boosts you bought separately are their own charge (the App Store lists 1 Server Boost at $4.99/mo and Nitro plus Boost bundles), so check them after cancelling Nitro. Nitro perks end when the paid period does. Discord says price varies by country and plan.

name: Dollar Shave Club
why: Razor and grooming shipments with no membership fee, but they keep coming on your set schedule. Stretch the interval or skip until your stockpile runs low.

rotate.pattern: Move shipments to every second or third month, or use Skip Order and Pause Subscription on the Next Box tab. Add products only when you run out, so blades are not piling up in a drawer.

cancel.howTo: Visit Subscriptions on your account page, find the subscription and select Cancel Subscription. If you run into trouble, the Club Pros support team says it will honor the request right away.
cancel.gotchas: Cancel at least one day before your order date to avoid an unwanted charge. There is no membership fee, only product charges. Skip Order and Pause Subscription on the Next Box tab are alternatives if you only need a break.

name: DoorDash DashPass
why: At $9.99/mo it saves delivery fees only if you order several times a month. Pause or cancel in slow months and restart when you need it; benefits run to the end of the billing period.

rotate.pattern: Cancel or pause DashPass in months you cook at home and restart in the months you order a lot. DoorDash lets you pause from the Manage DashPass page. Check whether a card benefit covers it before paying yourself.

cancel.howTo: Open the DoorDash app or doordash.com, tap your account icon, open Manage DashPass, tap Cancel Membership, choose a reason and confirm with Cancel DashPass. You get a confirmation email.
cancel.gotchas: Cancel at least 24 hours before the next scheduled payment. Benefits stay active until the billing period ends, but cancelling during a free trial ends them immediately. The same page offers Pause as an alternative. Some card-linked promotions (for example from certain credit cards) step up to the full price after the promo months.

name: Factor
why: Prepared meals billed weekly with a shipping fee on every delivery. Skip the weeks you will not eat them; changes are due about five days before delivery.

rotate.pattern: Order for busy stretches (a new job, a baby, travel prep) and skip the rest. Pick the smallest weekly meal count that covers your gap. Savings are modest because you still eat in the weeks you skip.

cancel.howTo: Log in on factor75.com or the app, open your account and plan settings, and choose pause or cancel. You can also skip individual deliveries from the Upcoming deliveries view.
cancel.gotchas: Factor says you can pause or cancel at any time, but changes are due about five days before delivery and the exact cutoff shows in your account. A shipping fee applies on every delivery. Menu labels may differ from these steps, so follow the on-screen prompts.

name: Grubhub+
why: Amazon Prime members get Grubhub+ free by linking accounts. If you pay from about $9.99/mo for it and also have Prime, you are paying twice for the same perk.

cancel.howTo: First link your Amazon Prime account to Grubhub using the Prime offer page. Grubhub then cancels your paid plan, and the Prime-based membership starts the day after your current billing cycle ends. Without Prime, cancel in your Grubhub account under the Grubhub+ membership settings or contact Grubhub support.
cancel.gotchas: The free Prime benefit ends the moment Prime ends and never converts to a paid plan on its own. Grubhub+ Credit from pickup expires 90 days after the most recent credit is issued and cannot be used on alcohol. Grubhub can change or end the Prime offer at any time. The paid plan is reported as starting at $9.99/mo and what you pay can be higher, so confirm it in the app.

name: HelloFresh
why: Weekly boxes plus a shipping fee, charged automatically unless you skip or pause by the cutoff. Skip weeks and pause between stretches instead of paying every week.

rotate.pattern: Order for a few weeks, skip or pause for a few, and come back when you want a reset. Set a calendar reminder for the skip cutoff, which is 11:59 pm PST five days before delivery. Savings are modest because you still buy groceries in the weeks you skip.

cancel.howTo: Log in, click your name > Account Settings, open Plan settings, scroll to Status and click Cancel Plan, then follow the prompts. To skip instead, select the delivery day and click Skip Week.
cancel.gotchas: Changes must be made by 11:59 pm PST, five days before the delivery or you pay for that box. Free add-ons from new-customer offers usually end if you cancel and may not return when you reactivate. The first-box offer does not cover shipping, upgrades or add-ons.

name: Hinge
why: Hinge+ and HingeX renew automatically with several price points on the App Store. Pay only during active periods and switch auto-renew off when you pause.

rotate.pattern: Buy the shortest term only while you are actively using Hinge, switch auto-renew off the same day you buy, and let it lapse during breaks. Longer plans look cheaper per month but renew automatically for the full term.

cancel.howTo: Cancel where you bought it: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > Hinge; Android Google Play > Subscriptions. Check the Hinge help center for web purchases.
cancel.gotchas: Deleting the app or your profile does not stop billing. The App Store lists subscription price points from $14.99 to $34.99, plus Boosts and Roses as separate purchases, and does not say how long each plan runs, so check the renewal date on your Apple or Google subscription page.

name: Home Chef
why: Weekly meal kits with a minimum order and shipping at checkout. Skip any week before the Friday noon CT cutoff, and note that 'pause' actually cancels the plan.

rotate.pattern: Keep the subscription but skip the weeks you will be away or eating out, from the Upcoming Orders page. Home Chef lets you skip any week without cancelling, so you only pay for the weeks you cook.

cancel.howTo: Log in, open Account > Account Settings and choose Pause My Account at the bottom of the left-hand tabs (in the app: Account > My Settings > Pause My Account). Despite the name this cancels the subscription, and it is complete only after the confirmation screen and email. Your first order is handled separately through support.
cancel.gotchas: Home Chef's support site says 'pause' actually cancels the subscription, which you can reactivate later. Deadlines are noon CT on the Friday before delivery; later changes are still billed. If you changed before the deadline and have timestamped proof, the terms promise a credit or refund within 30 days. Prices (about $9.99 a serving) and minimum orders vary by plan.

name: Instacart+
why: $9.99/mo or $99/yr waives delivery fees on orders over the minimum. It only pays off if you order often; the free trial auto-renews into the annual plan, so many people overpay.

rotate.pattern: Use the $9.99 monthly plan only in months with several big orders (holidays, a sick week, a new baby) and cancel after. Annual refunds are limited, so switch to monthly at your next renewal rather than mid-term.

cancel.howTo: In the Instacart app or on instacart.com open the menu or Account icon, choose Your Instacart+ membership, then Manage your membership > Cancel membership > Continue to cancel > Confirm cancellation. A confirmation email follows.
cancel.gotchas: The 14-day free trial auto-renews to the $99/year plan, not the monthly one. After cancelling, $0 delivery fees continue to the end of the billing period. Annual fees are refundable only if you cancel within 5 calendar days of the paid term and have placed no orders with the membership; otherwise there is no refund.

name: Match
why: Multi-month plans auto-renew at the then-current price. Buy the shortest term while active, turn off auto-renew right away, and cancel again when you stop dating.

rotate.pattern: Buy the shortest term only while you are actively using Match, switch auto-renew off the same day you buy, and let it lapse during breaks. Longer plans look cheaper per month but renew automatically for the full term.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at match.com, open Account Settings and the subscription or billing page, and turn off auto-renewal or cancel. If you bought through Apple or Google, cancel in those subscription settings.
cancel.gotchas: Longer plans renew for the full term at the current price unless you cancel before the renewal date, which is shown in account settings. Record any confirmation number or email. Prices vary by plan length and promotions, and no current US list price is confirmed on an official page.

name: Meta Verified
why: Badge, impersonation protection and support at $11.99/mo on web, $14.99 in the app, per profile. Worth it mainly for creators and small businesses; most individuals can cancel.

cancel.howTo: Cancel on the platform where you bought it: the subscription management screen in the Facebook or Instagram app, or Apple or Google subscription settings. The Meta Verified Help Center on Facebook or Instagram has the current menu path.
cancel.gotchas: Billing is per profile, so a Facebook and an Instagram subscription are separate charges. The web price ($11.99) is cheaper than the app price ($14.99), and the Plus ($49.99), Premium ($149.99) and Max ($499.99) tiers are app-only. Subscriptions renew automatically and the verified badge is removed when the subscription ends.

name: MyHeritage
why: Plans (Premium, Complete, PremiumPlus) renew automatically. Use it for a research push, export your tree as GEDCOM, then cancel; FamilySearch offers free records.

alternatives.name: FamilySearch
alternatives.note: Free genealogy records and family trees, no subscription.

rotate.pattern: Subscribe when you have a specific research goal, download matches and records, export your tree as a GEDCOM file, then cancel before the renewal date. Resubscribe when new leads come up.

cancel.howTo: Sign in, open your account settings, find your subscription and turn off auto-renewal. If you cannot find the option, use the contact form in the Help Center and keep the confirmation.
cancel.gotchas: Subscriptions renew automatically, so cancel before the renewal date. The pricing page lists plan names without amounts, so no US list price is confirmed. Check your own plan and price in account settings.

name: Patreon (memberships)
why: Each pledge is a separate charge to a creator you chose, so one line on your statement can hide several memberships. Keep the ones you value; review the list each quarter and cancel the rest.

cancel.howTo: Open Patreon, go to your memberships list, choose the creator, then edit or cancel the membership. Repeat for every creator you want to drop.
cancel.gotchas: Patreon bills each creator separately, usually at the start of the month for monthly pledges, so cancelling after the charge date does not undo that month. Purchases made on iOS or Android may be billed by Apple or Google instead. The statement line does not name the creator, so use Patreon billing history to match amounts.

name: Reddit Premium
why: Ad-free browsing and perks at $6.99/mo or $59.99/yr (App Store listing). Keep it if you are on Reddit daily; otherwise cancel and use the free site.

cancel.howTo: Cancel where you bought it: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > Reddit; Android Google Play > Subscriptions; web purchases from your Reddit account settings under Premium.
cancel.gotchas: Deleting the app does not cancel an Apple or Google subscription. Collectible avatars and Reddit Gold awards are one-off purchases that appear as separate charges. Web and app prices can differ, and no web price is confirmed on an official page.

name: Sam's Club
why: Club is $60/yr and Plus is $120/yr (raised May 2026). Plus now includes Walmart+, so drop a separate Walmart+ if you pay for both. A satisfaction-guarantee refund is available.

cancel.howTo: Cancel in a club, call 1-888-746-7726, or use your online account. Cancelling auto-renew is a separate step from cancelling the membership itself, so do both.
cancel.gotchas: Without a refund your access runs to the end of the membership year. The 100% satisfaction guarantee excludes sponsored or third-party memberships and memberships billed through Walmart. Only one Plus cancellation per household or business per year. Ask Sam's for the refund before disputing the charge with your card issuer.

name: Snapchat+
why: Snapchat+ at $4.99/mo (App Store) buys cosmetic and early-access perks such as custom icons, a badge and chat wallpapers. Cheap, so keep it if you use the perks; cancel when you stop.

cancel.howTo: Cancel where you bought it: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > Snapchat+; Android Google Play > Subscriptions. In the Snapchat app, open your profile and the Snapchat+ page to manage the subscription.
cancel.gotchas: Snapchat+ is separate from Memories storage plans and Snapstreak Restore purchases, which appear as their own App Store charges ($1.99 and $0.49 to $1.49 in the listing). Deleting the app does not cancel the subscription.

name: Telegram Premium
why: Telegram Premium is $4.99/mo or $35.99/yr (App Store listing) for bigger files and extra features. Keep it if you use the limits; the free app is fully usable otherwise.

name: The Athletic
why: Sports journalism that NYT All Access already includes. Check for a duplicate, then ask for a retention rate before the renewal date or cancel and read the free articles.

haggle.leverage: Annual pricing is cheaper than monthly, and retention discounts are commonly offered when you start to cancel. If you also hold an NYT All Access plan, the standalone Athletic plan is a duplicate and you can cancel it with no loss.
haggle.script: Hi, I subscribe to The Athletic and my plan is coming up for renewal. I enjoy the coverage but I'm trimming subscriptions, and the renewal price is higher than I'd like. Is there a discounted annual rate or retention offer available for the next year? If not, please cancel at the end of this billing period and send me a confirmation email so I know I won't be charged.
haggle.bestTime: One to two weeks before renewal. Offers are not guaranteed.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to your account, open subscription settings and choose Cancel. If your Athletic access comes through a NYT account, manage it there. If you subscribed through Apple or Google, cancel in those subscription settings.
cancel.gotchas: Reported standalone prices range from $7.99 to $9.99 a month, or $71.99 a year, and sources disagree, so check your own price in account settings. A NYT All Access bundle includes The Athletic. Some plans have 7-day free trials that auto-renew.

name: The Atlantic

name: Tinder
why: Plus, Gold and Platinum cost different amounts by plan length and region and auto-renew. Subscribe in short bursts while actively dating and switch off auto-renew right away.

rotate.pattern: Buy the shortest term only while you are actively using Tinder, switch auto-renew off the same day you buy, and let it lapse during breaks. Longer plans look cheaper per month but renew automatically for the full term.

cancel.howTo: Cancel where you bought it: iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions > Tinder; Android Google Play > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > Tinder; web purchases in your Tinder account settings under manage payment account.
cancel.gotchas: Deleting the app or your profile does not stop billing. The App Store shows several price points for Gold ($13.99 to $24.99) and Plus ($9.99), and one-off add-ons such as Boosts and Super Likes are separate charges. Prices vary by region and plan length.

name: Uber One
why: $9.99/mo covers delivery fees and ride perks. Worth it only if you use it a few times a month; otherwise end it and rejoin when needed. No refunds once a billing cycle has begun.

rotate.pattern: End Uber One after months with few orders or rides and rejoin the month you travel or order a lot. End it a couple of days before renewal, since fees are not refunded mid-cycle.

cancel.howTo: In the Uber app open the Uber One section, choose Manage Membership, then End Membership.
cancel.gotchas: Charges are non-refundable once a billing cycle begins. Uber Cash and credits earned through the membership may be lost when it ends.

name: Adobe Acrobat Pro
why: Most people merge, split, sign and fill PDFs. A private browser toolkit does that for free in an afternoon. Keep Acrobat only for true text editing, redaction or certified signatures.

alternatives.name: macOS Preview
alternatives.note: Built into every Mac: merge, reorder, annotate, fill forms and sign.

alternatives.name: PDFgear
alternatives.note: Free desktop PDF editor and converter.

alternatives.name: PDF24 Tools
alternatives.note: Free PDF tools, including merge, split, compress and OCR.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A private PDF toolkit that runs in the browser: merge, split, reorder, rotate and delete pages, fill forms, add text and signatures, compress by re-rendering pages as images, and OCR scans into searchable PDFs.
rebuild.runsOn: Installable PWA (pdf-lib, pdf.js, tesseract.js) hosted free on Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages; files never leave the device.
rebuild.youLose: True text editing inside existing PDFs, Adobe-grade redaction and accessibility tagging, certified digital signatures, and Acrobat's polish and support.
rebuild.prompt: Build me a private PDF toolkit as an installable PWA with no backend and no accounts. Stack: Vite, TypeScript, pdf-lib for editing, pdf.js for rendering, and tesseract.js for optional OCR, all running in the browser so files never leave my device. Core features: (1) merge several PDFs and drag to reorder pages, (2) split by page range or extract pages, (3) rotate and delete pages, (4) fill form fields and add typed or drawn signatures and text boxes, (5) compress by re-rendering pages as JPEG at a chosen quality, with a warning that this flattens text, (6) OCR a scanned PDF into a searchable one. Keep only a recent-files list of names in IndexedDB, never file contents. Include unit tests for merge, split and rotate using small sample PDFs. Deploy free to Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages and explain how to install it from the browser. Finish with a README listing what it cannot do compared with Acrobat Pro.

haggle.leverage: Cheaper tiers in the same family (Acrobat Standard $14.99, Acrobat Express $9.99) and free PDF tools. Adobe often shows a retention offer when you start cancelling.
haggle.script: Hi, I use Acrobat Pro mainly to merge, sign and fill PDFs, and at $19.99 a month it is more than I need. I am about to cancel. Can you move me to Acrobat Standard or apply a retention discount for the next term? Please confirm the new price, the term length, and whether any early termination fee applies to the change.
haggle.bestTime: Shortly before an annual term renews, via the cancel flow in your Adobe account or Adobe chat.

cancel.howTo: Adobe account, Plans, Manage plan for Acrobat, Cancel your plan, then confirm. Save any PDFs stored in Adobe cloud storage first.
cancel.gotchas: Annual billed monthly: half of the remaining commitment is charged if you cancel after 14 days. Annual prepaid: non-refundable after 14 days. Monthly ($29.99): no fee but the highest rate.

haggle.script: Hi, I am planning to cancel my Creative Cloud plan because it costs more than I use it for. I mostly use [APP]. Before I confirm, can you tell me what retention offers or lower-priced plans are available, such as the Photography plan, a single-app plan, or a discounted renewal for the next term? I would like to stay a customer if the price comes down. Please also confirm in writing the renewal price and term, and whether any early termination fee applies if I change plans.
haggle.bestTime: Two to four weeks before an annual term ends. Cancelling mid-term on an annual-billed-monthly plan after the first 14 days costs half of the remaining commitment, so time the call to the renewal date.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to your Adobe account, open Plans, choose Manage plan for the plan you want to end, select Cancel your plan, pick a reason and confirm. Each plan is cancelled separately.
cancel.gotchas: Annual-billed-monthly plans charge half the remaining commitment if you cancel after 14 days; prepaid annual plans are non-refundable after 14 days; month-to-month has no fee. Access continues to the end of the paid period. Plans bought through Apple, Google or Microsoft cancel there.

name: Babbel
why: Babbel's 12-month plan is $8.95 a month, or about $17.95 monthly. Claude can run similar dialogue, grammar and review drills, though you give up native-speaker audio and speech scoring.

alternatives.name: Duolingo Free
alternatives.note: Free tier with ads.

alternatives.name: Anki
alternatives.note: Free spaced-repetition flashcards.

absorb.claudeDoes: Writes a structured course with dialogues, vocabulary, grammar notes and exercises, then delivers one lesson at a time, grades your answers, tracks your errors and repeats weak points.
absorb.howTo: Start a Claude Project for the language, paste the course prompt below into the project instructions, and say next to get each lesson. Use voice mode on the phone to practice speaking.
absorb.limits: No recorded native-speaker audio, no speech recognition feedback, no polished app flow or progress screens, and you must keep the review list yourself. Claude can be wrong on rare languages and idioms.
absorb.prompt: Act as a course designer and tutor for [LANGUAGE] for an adult beginner. Create a 12-week plan with 4 lessons per week, each about 15 minutes. Each lesson has: a short dialogue with an English translation, 8 vocabulary items, one grammar point explained in plain English, and 5 exercises (fill in the blank, translation, and a mini role-play). Deliver one lesson only when I type next. After each lesson, grade my answers, show corrections with a short reason, and add every miss to a running Review list. Every fourth lesson, run a review that mixes the Review list with new material. Keep dialogues realistic for [travel / work / family] and tell me the weekly goal at the start of each week. Ask me to paste the Review list if the conversation is new.

rotate.pattern: Buy a 3- or 6-month plan when you start a new language or course, work through it, and let it lapse. Cancel auto-renewal on day one so it does not roll into another term.

cancel.howTo: Log in to your Babbel account, open Subscription, and turn off auto-renewal. If you bought through Apple or Google, cancel there.
cancel.gotchas: Plans are prepaid for 1, 3, 6 or 12 months and renew for the same term unless auto-renewal is turned off. Babbel advertises a money-back guarantee, so check its window.

name: Blinkist
why: Blinkist sells short summaries of nonfiction books. Claude summarizes books you name, paste or upload, adds critique and a quiz, so the paid tier is largely redundant once you pay for Claude.

alternatives.name: Libby
alternatives.note: Borrow the full book free with a library card.

absorb.claudeDoes: Summarizes nonfiction books into key ideas, examples, action steps and a quiz; critiques the argument; and for text you paste or upload, summarizes only what the text says.
absorb.howTo: Ask for a summary by title and author, or upload the PDF or paste chapters into a Claude Project. Claude Pro is $20 a month ($17 on annual billing) and Projects hold uploaded documents.
absorb.limits: From memory Claude can be vague or wrong about lesser-known or very recent books, so give it the text when accuracy matters. No curated library, no narrated audio, and no licensed publisher summaries.
absorb.prompt: Summarize [BOOK TITLE] by [AUTHOR] as a 15-minute read in the style of Blinkist. Give me: a one-sentence thesis, the 7 key ideas each with one concrete example from the book, 3 direct quotes only if you are certain they are accurate, 5 action steps I can try this week, and 2 places where the book is weak or contested. If you are not confident you know this book well, say so and ask me to paste the chapter titles or text instead. For text I paste or upload, summarize only what is in the text and mark anything you add from your own knowledge. Finish with a five-question quiz and wait for my answers before revealing the key.

cancel.howTo: Open your Blinkist account settings, go to Subscription, and cancel. If you subscribed through Apple or Google Play, cancel in that store.
cancel.gotchas: Blinkist is typically sold as a yearly plan charged in one payment after a free trial, so cancel before the trial ends. Check the renewal date and set a reminder.

name: Brilliant Premium
why: Brilliant is a sprint tool at $30 a month. Finish a course path in one or two months, then cancel. Claude can tutor the same math, science and computer science topics as part of a plan you already pay for.

alternatives.name: Khan Academy
alternatives.note: Free courses in math, science and computing.

alternatives.name: MIT OpenCourseWare
alternatives.note: Free university course materials.

rotate.pattern: Subscribe for one or two months to complete a single course path, cancel the day you start, and return for the next path. Annual billing only pays off if you use it most months.

absorb.claudeDoes: Teaches STEM topics one concept at a time, starting from a puzzle, asks you to predict first, explains the reasoning, generates practice problems and checks numbers by running code.
absorb.howTo: Put the prompt below in a Claude Project for your topic and ask for each session. Claude can run code to verify calculations and read photos of your handwritten work.
absorb.limits: No interactive visualizations or polished lesson flow, no progress tracking beyond what you paste back, and Claude can make arithmetic or reasoning errors, so ask it to verify by running code.
absorb.prompt: Teach me [TOPIC] the way Brilliant does. Build a four-week path of 20-minute sessions, three per week. For each session: start with a puzzle or question I can attempt before any explanation, ask me to predict the answer, then reveal the reasoning with a tiny worked example, then give a three-question check with increasing difficulty. Use code to verify any numbers before you state them. Keep a progress table (session, concept, score, weak spots) and print it at the end of every session so I can paste it back next time. If I get two checks wrong in a row, go back one step and explain differently. Use plain language and keep each message short.

cancel.howTo: Open your Brilliant account settings, go to Subscription and cancel. If you subscribed in the iPhone app, cancel in Apple subscriptions.
cancel.gotchas: Annual billing is advertised as saving 33 percent and renews yearly, so cancel before the renewal date. Family plans cover six seats and are cancelled by the owner.

cancel.gotchas: Free trials convert to paid automatically. After downgrading, replace Pro-only stock and elements in existing designs before you export. Team plans are billed per person.

name: Chegg Study Pack

examples: CHEGG* STUDY PACK SANTA CLARA CA

why: Claude explains homework step by step, checks your work and drafts study guides. Chegg's edge is expert-written textbook solutions; if you mostly use it for explanations, Claude covers it.

alternatives.name: Khan Academy
alternatives.note: Free lessons and practice in math, science and more.

absorb.claudeDoes: Explains homework problems step by step, gives hints before answers, reads photos of printed or handwritten work, checks numbers by running code, and writes practice problems and study guides.
absorb.howTo: Open a Claude chat or Project for the course, paste the problem or upload a photo, and use the tutor prompt below. Claude can run code to verify calculations.
absorb.limits: No access to your textbook's own solution set, and it can make arithmetic or reasoning errors, so verify results. Follow your school's academic-integrity rules and use it to learn, not to submit answers.
absorb.prompt: Act as my tutor for [COURSE]. When I paste a problem, do not give the answer first. Ask what I have tried, then give a hint. If I am still stuck, give a bigger hint, and only then show the full worked solution with each step explained in plain language. Verify final numbers by running code, and say so when you do. After each problem, give me one similar practice problem with a different setup and check my attempt. If I upload a photo, first restate what you read so I can confirm you read it correctly. At the end of the session, list the concepts I struggled with and suggest what to review. Remind me to cite my sources if I use your explanation in graded work.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to Chegg, open Account settings, find My subscriptions, and cancel Chegg Study Pack. Keep the confirmation email.
cancel.gotchas: Billing continues monthly until you cancel, so cancel before the renewal date. Check how many expert questions your plan allows each month against how much you actually use it.

name: Codecademy Plus

absorb.claudeDoes: Explains concepts, writes graded practice exercises with test cases, reviews your code, explains errors, and can scaffold small projects you then study and change.
absorb.howTo: Create a Claude Project for your language, paste the prompt below into the instructions, and work in your own editor. Claude Code is included with Claude Pro for project work.
absorb.limits: No in-browser auto-graded exercises, no certificates, career paths or interview simulations, and no progress dashboard. Claude can be confidently wrong, so run the code and tests yourself.
absorb.prompt: You are my coding tutor for [LANGUAGE]. My level is [beginner / some experience] and my goal is [build X / get a job]. Create a six-week syllabus with three sessions a week. In each session: explain one concept in under 150 words, show a tiny example, then give me three exercises of increasing difficulty with a test file I can run locally. Do not give the solution until I paste my attempt. When I paste code, review it for correctness, readability and one improvement, and explain any error message in plain language. Every second week, assign a small project and give me a rubric. Keep a Skills list of what I can do and what I keep missing, print it after each session, and ask me to paste it next time.

rotate.pattern: Pay monthly ($29.99) only when you want a certificate or a guided path, finish it in a month or two, and cancel. Use Claude or free curricula the rest of the year.

cancel.howTo: Sign in, open Settings, then Subscription, and cancel the plan. Plans bought through Apple or Google are cancelled in those stores.
cancel.gotchas: Annual plans renew yearly and free trials convert to paid. Cancel a day or more before the renewal date.

name: Coursera Plus
why: Coursera Plus is $59 monthly or $399 yearly. The yearly price equals about seven months, so pay monthly for the one or two months a certificate takes, then cancel. Many courses can be audited free.

alternatives.name: Audit courses free
alternatives.note: Many Coursera courses allow free audit access to lectures.

alternatives.name: edX audit
alternatives.note: Audit many university courses for free.

rotate.pattern: Start the 7-day trial, pick the specializations you want, pay $59 for one or two months to finish them and collect certificates, then cancel. Re-subscribe for the next batch.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to Coursera, open your account settings, go to Subscriptions or Purchases and cancel the Plus subscription. Confirm the cancellation email.
cancel.gotchas: The 7-day trial converts to paid. The annual plan has a 14-day money-back guarantee; the monthly plan does not list one on the page. Cancel at least a day before renewal.

name: DigitalOcean
why: A $6 droplet is cheap rented uptime. Keep it if anything public depends on it. If it only runs your own hobby services, a Raspberry Pi or old laptop at home with Tailscale and a tunnel replaces it.

alternatives.name: Oracle Cloud Always Free
alternatives.note: Free-tier VMs for small projects; availability and limits vary.

alternatives.name: Cloudflare Pages and Workers
alternatives.note: Free hosting for static sites and small edge functions.

selfhost.youLose: Datacenter uptime, a fixed public IP, fast symmetric bandwidth and DigitalOcean snapshots and support. Home power or ISP outages take your services down, and public access needs a tunnel rather than open router ports. The cost figure includes about $4 a year for the Backblaze B2 off-site copy of a small hobby setup.
selfhost.prompt: Help me move my hobby DigitalOcean droplet to a Raspberry Pi 5 at home running Raspberry Pi OS Lite 64-bit, or an old laptop running Ubuntu Server LTS. I will run you on the home machine and give you SSH access to the droplet. First inventory what runs on the droplet (docker ps, systemctl list-units, crontab, web server config) and write it to inventory.md. Then write a Docker Compose stack that reproduces it, with Caddy as the reverse proxy. For public access without opening router ports use a Cloudflare Tunnel; for private admin use Tailscale (free tier) with SSH reachable only over the tailnet. Configure unattended-upgrades, ufw and fail2ban, nightly encrypted restic backups to a USB drive, and an offsite copy to Backblaze B2. Add Uptime Kuma for health checks. Include a cutover plan: lower the DNS TTL, rsync the data, test on a temporary hostname, switch DNS, keep the droplet for seven days, then destroy it, because powered-off droplets still bill.

cancel.howTo: Destroy every droplet, volume, snapshot, floating IP and load balancer in the control panel, then confirm the billing page shows no active resources.
cancel.gotchas: Powering a droplet off does not stop billing; only destroying it does. Snapshots, volumes and reserved IPs bill separately. Download backups before destroying.

name: Duolingo Super/Max
why: Duolingo is free with ads. Paid tiers remove hearts and ads, and Max adds AI explanations and role-play that Claude does natively. Claude holds a conversation at your level and explains every mistake.

alternatives.name: Duolingo Free
alternatives.note: Free tier with ads and limited hearts.

alternatives.name: Anki
alternatives.note: Free spaced-repetition flashcards for vocabulary.

absorb.claudeDoes: Runs typed or spoken conversation practice in your target language at your level, corrects each mistake with a one-line reason, drills vocabulary, builds a weekly study plan and explains grammar on request.
absorb.howTo: Create a Claude Project for the language and put your level, goal and weekly time in the project instructions. Use voice mode on the mobile app for speaking practice. Claude Pro is $20 a month ($17 on annual billing).
absorb.limits: No streaks, XP, hearts or reminders, no fixed curriculum unless you write one into the project instructions, no pronunciation scoring, and non-English voice mode is still in beta. Claude can make mistakes in less common languages, so cross-check grammar rules.
absorb.prompt: You are my language tutor for [LANGUAGE]. My level is [A1/A2/B1/B2]. My goal is [travel / work / family] and I can study 20 minutes a day, five days a week. Start with a 10-question placement quiz, one question at a time. Then run a repeating session: (1) a five-minute recap of the words I missed last time, (2) a new topic with 8 to 10 words and example sentences, (3) a ten-minute conversation where you speak only [LANGUAGE] at my level and correct my mistakes after each reply, showing the corrected sentence and a one-line reason, (4) a five-question quiz. End every session with a list called Review words and ask me to paste it back at the start of the next one. If I type HELP, explain in English. Never write more than six lines unless I ask.

cancel.howTo: Web: Settings, Super or Max subscription, Manage subscription, Cancel. iPhone: Settings, your name, Subscriptions. Android: Google Play, Payments and subscriptions.
cancel.gotchas: Most subscribers are billed through Apple or Google, so deleting the app or your Duolingo account does not stop billing. A family plan is cancelled by its owner and ends for everyone.

name: Elevate

examples: ELEVATE LABS INC SAN FRANCISCO CA

why: Elevate sells daily word, math and memory drills at $39.99 a year. Few people keep up the daily habit. Free puzzle apps or a custom PWA give you the same practice.

alternatives.name: Elevate free version
alternatives.note: One three-game workout a day with basic tracking.

alternatives.name: Human Benchmark
alternatives.note: Free cognitive tests in the browser.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A daily practice PWA with vocabulary, spelling, mental math and reading-speed drills, adaptive difficulty, a daily three-game workout, streaks and stats.
rebuild.runsOn: Offline PWA on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages (free); progress in localStorage.
rebuild.youLose: Elevate's game variety and polish, its editorial content, benchmarks and syncing across devices. Your build covers fewer skills and has no scientific validation.
rebuild.prompt: Build a daily word-and-math practice PWA with no accounts. Four modes: vocabulary (pick the definition for a word from a JSON list of 300 words with definitions that you write and I can extend), spelling (hear the word with the browser speech synthesis, then type it), mental math (timed operations at five difficulty levels), and reading speed (a short passage followed by three questions; write 10 original passages in /content). A daily workout picks three modes and takes about ten minutes. Adjust difficulty per mode: harder after three correct in a row, easier after two misses. Track streaks, accuracy and weekly stats in localStorage, with a simple chart. Use Vite and TypeScript, an installable manifest, offline support, large touch targets and a reduce-motion setting. Add tests for the scoring and difficulty logic. Host free on GitHub Pages.

cancel.howTo: Elevate bills through the App Store. On iPhone open Settings, tap your name, Subscriptions, choose Elevate and cancel. Deleting the app does not cancel the subscription.
cancel.gotchas: The annual plan includes a 7-day free trial that converts to paid. The monthly plan has no trial. Cancel at least 24 hours before renewal.

name: Figma Professional
why: Few tools match Figma's shared libraries and Dev Mode. If you only review or comment on files, a Collab seat at $3 or the free Starter plan (three design files) is enough.

alternatives.name: Penpot
alternatives.note: Open-source design and prototyping tool, free to self-host or use hosted.

alternatives.name: Figma Starter
alternatives.note: Free plan, limited to one team and three design files.

cancel.howTo: Open the team in Figma, go to Settings, Billing, and downgrade the team to Starter. The paid plan runs to the end of the billing period.
cancel.gotchas: Starter allows only three design files and one team, so export .fig copies of everything else before downgrading. Extra seats, including Dev and Collab seats, are billed separately.

name: GitHub Pro
why: GitHub Free already includes unlimited private repositories and 2,000 CI minutes a month. Pro adds protected branches, required reviewers and more Codespaces hours, which most solo developers never use.

alternatives.name: GitHub Free
alternatives.note: Unlimited public and private repos, 2,000 CI/CD minutes a month.

alternatives.name: Codeberg
alternatives.note: Non-profit, open-source Git hosting.

cancel.howTo: Open GitHub Settings, then Billing and licensing, then Additional billing details. Under Current plan open the Edit menu, choose Downgrade to Free and confirm. The downgrade takes effect on your next billing date.
cancel.gotchas: Private-repo features such as protected branches and required reviewers stop applying after the downgrade. GitHub Copilot is a separate subscription and must be cancelled on its own.

name: GoDaddy
why: First-year prices are teasers; renewals, privacy and email add-ons cost more. Ask for a renewal coupon and drop unused add-ons, or transfer the domain to a registrar that charges closer to cost.

alternatives.name: Cloudflare Registrar
alternatives.note: Sells domains at wholesale cost with free WHOIS privacy.

alternatives.name: Namecheap
alternatives.note: Domains with free privacy protection for life.

alternatives.name: Porkbun
alternatives.note: Low renewal prices with free WHOIS privacy.

haggle.leverage: A transfer quote from Cloudflare, Namecheap or Porkbun for the same domain, and the add-ons you can drop (privacy, email, website builder). GoDaddy support can apply promo codes on renewal.
haggle.script: Hi, my domain [DOMAIN] renews on [DATE] at [PRICE]. I have a quote of [PRICE] to transfer it to another registrar, and I would rather stay if you can come closer. Can you apply a renewal discount or promo code and remove the add-ons I do not use, such as [PRIVACY / EMAIL / WEBSITE BUILDER]? Please confirm the final total and renewal term by email before I agree.
haggle.bestTime: Two to four weeks before the renewal date, through chat or phone support.

cancel.howTo: In your GoDaddy account open Renewals and Billing, turn off auto-renew on each product, and cancel add-ons. To keep the domain, unlock it, request the authorization code and transfer it to another registrar.
cancel.gotchas: Each product renews separately, so cancelling the domain does not cancel hosting, email or a website builder. Domains registered or transferred in the last 60 days usually cannot be transferred out.

name: Google Workspace
why: Business Starter is $7 per user a month with a one-year commitment and is the simplest custom-domain email with Drive and Meet. Free email routing plus Gmail works for one person who can skip admin features.

alternatives.name: Cloudflare Email Routing
alternatives.note: Free forwarding of you@yourdomain to a Gmail inbox; pair with Gmail Send mail as.

alternatives.name: Proton Mail Free
alternatives.note: Free encrypted mailbox, custom domains need a paid plan.

cancel.howTo: As an admin, open the Admin console, Billing, Subscriptions, select the Workspace subscription and choose Cancel subscription. Export mail and files first with the data export tool or Google Takeout.
cancel.gotchas: Cancelling removes user data after a grace period, and mail to your domain stops working until you point MX records elsewhere. Domain registration is billed separately from Workspace.

name: Headway
why: Headway renews at double its intro price: $79.98 every 12 weeks, about $29 a month. Claude summarizes nonfiction books you name or paste and can run flashcards, so the paid app is easy to replace.

alternatives.name: Libby
alternatives.note: Borrow the full book free with a library card.

alternatives.name: Anki
alternatives.note: Free spaced-repetition flashcards for key ideas.

absorb.claudeDoes: Builds a weekly reading plan from your book list, summarizes each book into key ideas, and quizzes you with spaced-repetition-style flashcards across sessions.
absorb.howTo: Create a Claude Project called Reading, paste the prompt below into its instructions, and add one book per week. Upload the text or paste chapters when accuracy matters.
absorb.limits: No audio summaries or app notifications, no curated catalog of 1,700 titles, and Claude can be vague about obscure or recent books. Spaced repetition only works if you return and paste your card list.
absorb.prompt: Act as my reading coach. I will give you a nonfiction book title and author each week. For each book: (1) write a 15-minute summary with the thesis, 7 key ideas, and one example per idea, (2) turn the ideas into 12 flashcards in the format Question | Answer, (3) give each card a review interval (next day, three days, one week, one month) and list the cards in a table I can paste back later. At the start of each conversation, ask me to paste my card list and my scores, then quiz me on cards that are due. Mark the cards I miss and show them more often. If you are not confident you know a book well, say so and ask me to paste text. Never invent quotes. Keep every answer short.

cancel.howTo: Cancel in your Headway account or in the app store where you subscribed. Email support@get-headway.com if you cannot find the option, and keep the confirmation.
cancel.gotchas: Plans run 4, 12 or 24 weeks, not months. The intro price (for example $39.99 for 12 weeks) renews at double ($79.98). Cancel at least 24 hours before renewal.

name: JetBrains IDEs
why: For daily professional work the IDEs earn their price. Hobby and open-source use may qualify for a free licence, and a paid subscription earns a perpetual fallback licence after 12 months.

alternatives.name: Visual Studio Code
alternatives.note: Free editor with extensions for nearly every language.

alternatives.name: Zed
alternatives.note: Fast free editor with built-in collaboration.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to your JetBrains Account, open Subscriptions, and turn off automatic renewal. You keep working until the paid term ends.
cancel.gotchas: A yearly subscription, or 12 consecutive monthly renewals, earns a perpetual fallback licence for the version you had, so cancelling does not lock you out of it. Missing a monthly renewal before month 12 forfeits the fallback. Stopping can also reset the continuity discount.

name: LinkedIn Premium
why: Premium pays off during a job search or a sales push, not as a year-round habit. Free LinkedIn covers networking. Subscribe for the months you are actively applying or prospecting.

alternatives.name: LinkedIn Free
alternatives.note: Free profile, messaging with connections and job search.

rotate.pattern: Subscribe when you begin an active job search or outreach push, use InMail and applicant insights, and cancel when you land the role or the push ends. Use the free trial once, then pay monthly only when needed.

cancel.howTo: Open LinkedIn, then Me, Settings and Privacy, Subscriptions and payments, Manage Premium account, and choose Cancel subscription.
cancel.gotchas: Free trials convert to paid unless cancelled. Cancelling keeps Premium until the period ends, and the flow may show a discounted continuation offer. Subscriptions bought through Apple or Google cancel there.

name: Lumosity

examples: LUMOS LABS INC SAN FRANCISCO CA

why: Evidence that brain games improve everyday skills is thin, and Lumosity's maker agreed to a $2M FTC settlement in 2016 over its claims. If you just enjoy the games, a free PWA of your own is a weekend build.

alternatives.name: Lumosity Free
alternatives.note: Limited free daily workouts.

alternatives.name: Human Benchmark
alternatives.note: Free reaction, memory and typing tests.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A brain-games PWA with five games (n-back, memory grid, reaction time, mental arithmetic, Stroop), daily 10-minute workouts, adaptive difficulty, streaks and weekly charts.
rebuild.runsOn: Installable offline PWA on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages (free); scores in IndexedDB.
rebuild.youLose: Lumosity's dozens of designed games, tuned difficulty, benchmarks against other users and the research team behind them. Your build will be simpler and has no proven training effect.
rebuild.prompt: Build a brain-games PWA with no accounts and no tracking, and ask me what to name it before you start. Five games: n-back (levels 1 to 4), memory grid (flash a pattern, then recall it), reaction-time tap test, mental arithmetic sprint, and a Stroop color-word test. A daily workout picks three games and takes about ten minutes. Use adaptive difficulty: raise the level above 85 percent accuracy and lower it below 60 percent. Store scores, streaks and personal bests in IndexedDB, show a weekly chart per game, and work fully offline. Use Vite and TypeScript with plain DOM or Canvas, large touch targets, a reduce-motion setting and an installable manifest. Include tests for the difficulty adjustment logic. Host free on GitHub Pages. Write a README that is honest that brain games have limited evidence of improving everyday skills.

cancel.howTo: Sign in, open Account, then Subscription, and turn off renewal. If you subscribed in the iPhone or Android app, cancel in Apple subscriptions or Google Play.
cancel.gotchas: Subscriptions renew automatically. Look for the cancel option in Account settings before you contact support, and cancel at least a day before the renewal date.

name: MasterClass
why: MasterClass is a video catalog sold mostly as annual memberships, so a forgotten renewal costs a full year. Join when several classes appeal to you, turn off renewal right away, and return when new ones ship.

alternatives.name: Your library's digital services
alternatives.note: Libby offers free books, audiobooks and sometimes learning video through a library card.

rotate.pattern: Let the annual plan lapse after you finish your list. Re-subscribe when a new class you want ships, ideally during a sale, then turn off renewal right away.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to MasterClass, open Account, then Membership, and turn off auto-renew or cancel the membership.
cancel.gotchas: Memberships are annual and renew automatically. The site advertises a satisfaction guarantee on new purchases, so check its length. Set a reminder two weeks before renewal. Memberships bought through Apple are cancelled in Apple subscriptions.

name: Medium Membership

examples: MEDIUM MONTHLY MEMBERSHIP SAN FRANCISCO CA

why: At $5 a month Medium costs $60 a year for a reading list you can work through in a month or two. Pay for the months you read member-only stories and pause the rest.

alternatives.name: Writers' own newsletters
alternatives.note: Many Medium writers also publish free or paid newsletters.

rotate.pattern: Save member-only links in a reading list. Subscribe for a month when the list is long, read through it, then cancel. Re-subscribe when the list refills.

cancel.howTo: Go to Medium, open your profile menu, Membership, and choose Cancel membership. Access stays until the period ends.
cancel.gotchas: Check the refund terms before renewing an annual plan. If you joined through the iOS app, cancel in Apple subscriptions. Friend of Medium is $15 a month, so check which tier you are on.

name: Microsoft 365 Personal/Family
why: Personal is $99.99 a year ($9.99 monthly) and Family $129.99 ($12.99) for up to six people. Family split across a household is the best value; a solo user who only needs basic documents can use free web Office.

alternatives.name: Office on the web
alternatives.note: Free Word, Excel and PowerPoint in the browser with a Microsoft account.

alternatives.name: LibreOffice
alternatives.note: Free desktop office suite that opens and saves Office files.

alternatives.name: Google Docs
alternatives.note: Free browser-based documents and spreadsheets.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at account.microsoft.com/services, find Microsoft 365, choose Manage, then Cancel subscription or turn off recurring billing. Access continues until the end date.
cancel.gotchas: The free month converts to paid unless cancelled. After the plan ends, OneDrive drops to the free 5 GB tier, so move files off first. Subscriptions bought through Apple, Google or a carrier are cancelled there.

name: Namecheap
why: A .com renews at $19.98 a year with free privacy protection, already low. Cloudflare Registrar sells at cost if you hold several domains. Watch hosting and email add-ons, which renew separately.

alternatives.name: Cloudflare Registrar
alternatives.note: Wholesale-cost domains with free privacy.

alternatives.name: Porkbun
alternatives.note: Low renewals and free WHOIS privacy.

cancel.howTo: In your Namecheap account open Domain List, choose Manage, and switch Auto-Renew off. To leave, unlock the domain and transfer it out with the authorization code.
cancel.gotchas: An expired domain enters a redemption period that costs extra to recover. Private email, hosting and SSL add-ons renew on their own schedules, so turn those off separately.

name: Netlify Personal/Pro
why: Personal is $9 a month for 1,000 credits against 300 on the free plan. Most personal sites fit the free plan or a free static host. Keep it only if you actually run out of credits.

alternatives.name: Netlify Free
alternatives.note: Free plan with 300 credits a month.

alternatives.name: Cloudflare Pages
alternatives.note: Free static hosting with generous limits.

cancel.howTo: In the Netlify app open Team settings, Billing, and change the plan to Free. Check this month's credit usage first.
cancel.gotchas: Netlify now meters usage in credits. On Free, sites can stop serving when credits run out, so confirm your usage fits 300 credits before downgrading. Pro is a flat $20 per team.

name: Parallels Desktop
why: UTM is free and VMware Fusion has a personal-use licence; both run Windows or Linux on Apple silicon. Parallels wins on polish and graphics. Standard can also be bought outright, not renewed yearly.

alternatives.name: UTM
alternatives.note: Free, open-source virtual machines for Mac, runs Windows and Linux.

alternatives.name: VMware Fusion Pro
alternatives.note: Offered free for personal use at the time of writing; check the licence.

cancel.howTo: Turn off auto-renewal in your Parallels account under Subscriptions, or in Apple subscriptions if you bought through the Mac App Store. Keep Windows VMs by exporting or switching them to another hypervisor first.
cancel.gotchas: A promotional price on the buy page may not be the renewal price, so check what your account will charge. The Standard edition is also sold as a one-time purchase. Purchases carry a 30-day money-back guarantee.

name: Photomath Plus
why: Photomath lists step-by-step explanations on its free tier too, and Claude reads a photo of a problem and explains each step. Paying $9.99 monthly or $69.99 yearly is hard to justify.

alternatives.name: Photomath Basic
alternatives.note: Free tier with step-by-step explanations.

alternatives.name: Khan Academy
alternatives.note: Free lessons and practice in math.

absorb.claudeDoes: Reads photos of printed or handwritten math problems, explains each step in plain language, checks the answer by running code, and generates similar practice problems.
absorb.howTo: Upload a photo in the Claude mobile app and use the prompt below. Claude can run code to confirm calculations.
absorb.limits: No instant camera overlay scan, so each problem takes a few seconds more. Claude can misread messy handwriting or small text and can slip on arithmetic, so ask it to verify with code and restate the problem first.
absorb.prompt: You are my math tutor. When I upload a photo of a problem, first write out exactly what you read so I can confirm it. Then solve it step by step, explaining why each step is valid in plain language and naming the rule or property used. Verify the final answer by running code or substituting back, and say which you did. If the problem has more than one method, show the simplest first and mention the other in one sentence. After the solution, give me one similar problem with different numbers and check my attempt when I send it. If my handwriting is unclear, ask me to retake the photo instead of guessing. Keep explanations short unless I ask for more.

cancel.howTo: Subscriptions are managed where you bought them. On iPhone open Settings, your name, Subscriptions. On Android open Google Play, Payments and subscriptions. Web purchases are managed in your Photomath account.
cancel.gotchas: Deleting the app does not cancel a subscription. The annual plan renews yearly at full price and trials convert to paid unless cancelled.

name: Pluralsight

priceHints.plan: Individual annual plan (AI+, Cloud+, Security+, Data+ tier)
Individual annual plan (Core Tech or Complete tier)

why: Individual plans (Core Tech, AI+, Cloud+, Security+, Data+, Complete) are video libraries. Pay for the months you are studying for a certification or a new stack, then cancel.

alternatives.name: freeCodeCamp
alternatives.note: Free curriculum with projects and certifications.
