alternatives.name: Your library's digital services
alternatives.note: Many libraries offer free learning resources through a library card.

rotate.pattern: Use the free trial first. Subscribe for the months when you are preparing for a certification or learning a new stack, finish the path, then cancel and return for the next one.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to Pluralsight, open your account settings and subscription or plan section, and cancel renewal. Keep the confirmation email.
cancel.gotchas: Free trials convert to paid. Annual plans renew yearly, so set a reminder before the renewal date and check which individual plan (Core Tech, AI+, Cloud+, Complete) you are on.

name: Quizlet Plus
why: Plus is $35.99 a year for ad-free studying and limited practice tests. Flashcards with spaced repetition are a weekend build, and Claude can write the cards and quiz you. Anki already does this free.

alternatives.name: Anki
alternatives.note: Free, open-source spaced-repetition flashcards.

alternatives.name: Quizlet Free
alternatives.note: Free flashcards with ads and limited modes.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A flashcard PWA with decks, spaced-repetition scheduling, flip, type-answer, multiple-choice and matching modes, a daily due queue, stats, and import from Quizlet exports.
rebuild.runsOn: Offline PWA on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages (free); decks in IndexedDB with JSON export.
rebuild.youLose: Quizlet's huge library of public sets, class sharing and live games, textbook solutions and cross-device sync unless you add your own export and import.
rebuild.prompt: Build a flashcard PWA with spaced repetition, no accounts and no backend. Features: (1) decks and cards with text and optional images stored in IndexedDB, (2) FSRS or SM-2 scheduling with a daily due queue and a new-cards-per-day limit, (3) study modes: flip, type the answer, multiple choice built from other cards in the deck, and a timed matching game, (4) stats: streak, retention rate and a heatmap of reviews, (5) import from a Quizlet export pasted as text, with a tab between term and definition and a new line between cards, plus CSV and JSON import and export, (6) dark mode and keyboard shortcuts. Use Vite and TypeScript, make it installable and offline-capable, and add tests for the scheduler. Host free on GitHub Pages and explain how I back up my decks.

absorb.claudeDoes: Turns your notes into flashcards, quizzes you one card at a time, retests the cards you miss and writes practice tests with an answer key.
absorb.howTo: Paste your notes or upload a PDF into a Claude Project and run the prompt below. Ask for a fresh set before each exam.
absorb.limits: No automatic spaced-repetition scheduling or stats, no shared class sets, and you must paste the missed-card list back between sessions. Claude can make factual errors in cards, so check against your source.
absorb.prompt: Make me a study set from the notes I paste below. First write 25 flashcards in the format term | definition, focusing on the most testable points. Then quiz me one card at a time: show the term, wait for my answer, mark it right or wrong with a one-line correction, and keep a list of missed cards. Re-test each missed card after five other cards, and again at the end. When we finish, print the missed cards as a list I can paste next session, then write a ten-question practice test with an answer key that mixes multiple choice and short answer. If my notes are unclear on a point, ask me instead of guessing.

cancel.howTo: Sign in, open Settings, then Subscription, and cancel renewal. Plans bought in the iOS or Android app cancel in Apple subscriptions or Google Play.
cancel.gotchas: The 7-day trial applies to annual plans only and converts to a full-year charge. Annual plans renew automatically every year until cancelled. Export your sets on the website first: set menu (three dots) > Export > Copy text, one set at a time. Sets copied from other users cannot be exported, and sets that use Plus features may need Plus to copy. Keep the paid plan until the import is verified.

name: Rosetta Stone
why: Rosetta Stone is $19.99 monthly or $159 a year for 25 languages. It overlaps Duolingo and Babbel; its edge is TruAccent speech scoring. Without that need, free tools and Claude practice cover it.

alternatives.name: Duolingo Free
alternatives.note: Free tier with ads.

alternatives.name: Anki
alternatives.note: Free spaced-repetition flashcards for vocabulary.

absorb.claudeDoes: Runs immersion-style practice with short scene descriptions instead of pictures, asks you questions in the target language only, corrects errors and escalates difficulty.
absorb.howTo: Create a Claude Project for the language and use the prompt below as the instructions. Use voice mode on the phone for speaking turns; non-English voice support is in beta.
absorb.limits: No TruAccent pronunciation scoring, no image-based lessons, no structured units and no progress dashboard. Claude may miss subtle pronunciation problems, since it responds to your words, not your accent.
absorb.prompt: Teach me [LANGUAGE] by immersion. Use only [LANGUAGE] unless I type HELP. Each lesson has: (1) six new words introduced through a short scene description in simple [LANGUAGE] (for example, someone ordering coffee), (2) three questions about the scene that I answer in [LANGUAGE], (3) a build-a-sentence exercise using the new words, and (4) a three-turn dialogue with you. When I make a mistake, repeat my sentence corrected, then ask me to say it again. Raise difficulty after two clean lessons. After each lesson, print a Review list of words I missed and ask me to paste it back next time. Keep every message under eight lines and never translate unless I type HELP.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to your Rosetta Stone account, open Subscription settings and turn off automatic renewal. If that option is missing, contact Rosetta Stone support and ask for written confirmation.
cancel.gotchas: Yearly plans renew for another year unless you turn renewal off, so note the date. Lifetime purchases do not renew. Check your receipt email for the term and price you actually bought.

name: Setapp
why: At $14.99 a month for one Mac it pays off only if you use three or more of its apps regularly. Otherwise subscribe for the month you need an app, export your work, and cancel.

alternatives.name: Homebrew casks
alternatives.note: Install many free and open-source Mac apps from the command line.

rotate.pattern: Subscribe in a month when you need two or more Setapp apps for a project, finish and export the work, then cancel. Re-subscribe when the next project needs them. The 7-day trial is free on each plan.

cancel.howTo: Open your Setapp account, go to Subscription, and cancel the plan. Setapp apps stop opening when the paid period ends.
cancel.gotchas: The 7-day trial converts to paid monthly billing. Export documents from Setapp apps before the end date because they no longer launch afterwards.

name: Skillshare
why: Skillshare is a catalog of project classes that take weeks, not a year. Use the 7-day free trial, then subscribe for a month or two when you have classes queued, and cancel before it renews.

alternatives.name: YouTube tutorials
alternatives.note: Free tutorials for most creative software and skills.

alternatives.name: Your library's digital services
alternatives.note: Many libraries bundle free learning video through a library card.

rotate.pattern: Queue the classes you want, start the free 7-day trial, finish them, then pay for one more month only if needed and cancel immediately. Come back when the next list is ready.

cancel.howTo: On skillshare.com open Account settings, choose Membership and Payments, click Cancel membership and follow the prompts. On a phone, do it in the mobile browser, not the app, unless you subscribed through the app store.
cancel.gotchas: The free trial charges your card unless you cancel first. Skillshare does not refund renewals, and a 7-day trial charge is refundable only if you contact support within 48 hours and have not used the service. App-store subscriptions cancel in Apple or Google settings.

name: Squarespace
why: A portfolio or small business site is mostly static pages. Claude Code builds one in a day and free hosts serve it. You keep paying only for the domain. Stores and bookings are the exception.

alternatives.name: Cloudflare Pages
alternatives.note: Free static hosting with a custom domain.

alternatives.name: GitHub Pages
alternatives.note: Free static hosting from a repository.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A static personal or portfolio site with Home, About, Work, Blog and Contact pages, content in Markdown, RSS, sitemap and social-preview tags, deployed to free hosting on your own domain.
rebuild.runsOn: Astro static site on Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages (free). Only the domain costs money.
rebuild.youLose: The drag-and-drop editor (you edit Markdown or ask Claude), built-in forms, email campaigns, scheduling and commerce, analytics dashboards, template polish and support. If you sell products, keep Squarespace.
rebuild.prompt: Build my personal website as a static site I can host free. Use Astro with plain CSS and no CMS. Pages: Home, About, Work (a grid of projects from Markdown files with cover image, title, date and description), Blog (Markdown posts with tags and an RSS feed), and Contact (a mailto link plus an optional form endpoint I can swap in later). Requirements: responsive and accessible, light and dark mode, optimized images, sitemap.xml, Open Graph and Twitter card tags, and a 404 page. Put all content in /content as Markdown with frontmatter so I can edit it in any text editor. Before you start, ask me for my site name, tagline, accent color and my current site URL. Then fetch that URL's sitemap.xml and list the old URLs for the redirects. Walk me through deploying to Cloudflare Pages from a GitHub repository and attaching my existing domain. End with a checklist for exporting my Squarespace text and images before I cancel.

cancel.howTo: Open Settings, Billing and Account, Billing, then Subscriptions, select the site's plan and cancel it. Domains and Google Workspace are billed separately and must be cancelled or transferred on their own.
cancel.gotchas: Annual plans include a free domain for the first year only and renew at standard rates after that. Refund windows after purchase or renewal are short, so read the terms before you buy annual.

name: Vercel Pro
why: Pro is $20 per developer seat with a $20 usage credit, and Hobby is free but personal and non-commercial only. Keep it for commercial projects; hobby sites can move to Hobby or free static hosts.

alternatives.name: Cloudflare Pages
alternatives.note: Free static and edge hosting for personal and commercial sites.

alternatives.name: GitHub Pages
alternatives.note: Free static hosting straight from a repository.

cancel.howTo: In the Vercel dashboard open your team, go to Settings, Billing, and downgrade or cancel the Pro plan. Remove extra seats first.
cancel.gotchas: Hobby is for personal, non-commercial use only, so a commercial project must move host rather than downgrade. Usage beyond the credit is billed on Pro; check usage before cancelling.

name: Wix
why: A brochure site on the Light plan is a few static pages. Claude Code can rebuild it from your live pages and free hosts serve it, leaving only the domain cost. Keep Wix if you rely on bookings or a store.

alternatives.name: Cloudflare Pages
alternatives.note: Free static hosting with a custom domain.

alternatives.name: GitHub Pages
alternatives.note: Free static hosting from a repository.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A static copy of your Wix site: the same pages, text, images and navigation rebuilt in Astro, with a contact link, SEO tags, a sitemap and redirects from every old URL.
rebuild.runsOn: Astro static site on Cloudflare Pages (free) with your domain.
rebuild.youLose: Wix's editor, bookings, store, members area, built-in forms and email marketing, and one-click support. Wix has no full export, so Claude rebuilds from your published pages and downloaded images.
rebuild.prompt: I am replacing my Wix site with a static site hosted free. First ask me for my current Wix site URL, brand colors and fonts, and offer to read the colors and fonts from the live CSS. Then fetch its sitemap.xml and every page it lists, extract the text, headings and image URLs into Markdown files, and download the images into /public/images with descriptive file names. If a page needs JavaScript to show its content, tell me and I will paste the text. Rebuild the layout with Astro and plain CSS: header navigation, hero, content sections, a contact page with a mailto link, and a footer. Match those colors and fonts and the order of sections on each page. Add SEO basics: title and meta description per page, sitemap.xml, Open Graph tags, and a redirects file mapping every old Wix URL to its new path. Use Cloudflare Pages for hosting and walk me through moving my domain DNS. List anything you could not copy, such as bookings, a store or forms.

cancel.howTo: In Wix, open Billing and Payments, then Subscriptions, select the plan and cancel it. Domains are separate subscriptions and need their own cancellation or transfer.
cancel.gotchas: The free domain voucher applies to the first year of a first Premium purchase and the domain renews at regular price afterwards. Cancelling a site plan does not cancel the domain, and the refund window after purchase is short.

name: Wolfram|Alpha Pro
why: Pro is $5 a month billed yearly and adds step-by-step solutions, file uploads and longer computations. Claude explains steps and runs Python to compute exactly; you lose Wolfram's curated data.

alternatives.name: Wolfram|Alpha (free)
alternatives.note: The free tier answers most one-off questions.

alternatives.name: Desmos
alternatives.note: Free graphing calculator.

absorb.claudeDoes: Solves and explains algebra, calculus and statistics problems step by step, runs Python in its sandbox for exact computation and plots, and reads photos of problems.
absorb.howTo: Ask in a Claude chat or Project and tell it to verify results with code. Claude can run code and create files such as charts and spreadsheets.
absorb.limits: No access to Wolfram's curated, computable data (chemistry, geography, finance and more). Python's sympy covers most school-level symbolic work but not everything Wolfram's engine solves. Claude can make errors, so ask it to verify with code and double-check important results.
absorb.prompt: Act as a math and science problem solver. For each problem I give you: (1) restate it and list the givens, (2) solve step by step and name the method, (3) verify the result independently by running Python (use sympy or numpy where helpful) and show the code and its output, (4) state any assumptions or domain restrictions, and (5) if there is a plot that helps, produce it. If a result depends on data you cannot get reliably, say so instead of estimating. For symbolic work, give the exact form first and a decimal approximation second. If two methods disagree, show both and explain which one is correct. Keep explanations plain and short.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to your Wolfram account, open your subscriptions, and cancel Wolfram|Alpha Pro. Plans bought in the iOS or Android app cancel in the store.
cancel.gotchas: Annual subscriptions renew automatically. Student and educator plans have separate pricing, so check which plan you are on.

name: WordPress.com

examples: AUTOMATTIC INC* WPCOM SAN FRANCISCO CA

why: Personal is $4 a month on yearly billing ($9 if paid monthly), so savings are small. Keep it, or move the blog to a static site on free hosting if you want to stop paying anything beyond the domain.

alternatives.name: WordPress.com Free
alternatives.note: Free plan with a wordpress.com address and 1 GB of storage.

alternatives.name: Astro blog starter
alternatives.note: Free static blog templates you can host on Cloudflare Pages.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A static blog converted from your WordPress export: posts and pages as Markdown, images downloaded locally, tag pages, RSS, search and redirects that preserve your old permalinks.
rebuild.runsOn: Astro static site on Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages (free) with your domain.
rebuild.youLose: The WordPress editor and plugins, comments, built-in stats, email subscribers and the one-click admin. You write in Markdown and publish with git.
rebuild.prompt: I want to move my WordPress.com blog to a static site on free hosting. Start from the WXR export file that I will place in this folder as export.xml. Write a script that converts posts and pages to Markdown with frontmatter (title, date, tags, categories, slug), downloads every referenced image into /public/uploads and rewrites the links, and keeps the old permalink structure through a redirects file. Then build the site with Astro: post list with pagination, tag pages, an RSS feed at /feed.xml, full-text search with Pagefind, dark mode, and an About page. Comments are dropped; note how I could add giscus later. Deploy to Cloudflare Pages with my domain, leave email with its current provider, and give me a checklist for cancelling the WordPress.com plan only after DNS is switched and the new site is verified.

cancel.howTo: Open WordPress.com, go to Me, Purchases, select the plan and choose Cancel plan. Domains are listed as separate purchases.
cancel.gotchas: Refund windows are short (about two weeks for plans, shorter for domains). Monthly billing costs more than twice the yearly rate. Export your content from Tools, Export before downgrading.

name: 1Password
why: Password managers are not worth rebuilding or self-hosting. Individual is $3.99/mo regular ($2.99 promo for the first year). Bitwarden Premium at about $19.80 a year is the cheaper swap.

alternatives.name: Bitwarden
alternatives.note: Free plan with unlimited passwords and devices; Premium is $19.80 a year.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at 1password.com, open your account profile and the Billing or Subscription page, and cancel the membership. If you subscribed through the App Store or Google Play, cancel there instead.
cancel.gotchas: The $2.99 promotional price applies to new customers paying annually on 1Password.com for the first year, and is not offered through app stores. Export or move your vault before cancelling, and check 1Password's current rules for what access remains after a subscription lapses.

name: Abode

examples: ABODE SYSTEMS INC PALO ALTO CA

why: Abode has a free tier, a Standard tier and a Pro tier with 24/7 professional monitoring, with no contracts. Keep Pro only if you want dispatch; the cheaper tiers cover app control and video.

cancel.howTo: Open the Abode app, go to your plan settings and switch to a lower plan or cancel Pro. Abode says you can change plans at any time from the app. Camera-only video ($3.99 a month per camera) and 24/7 video storage ($9.99 a month) are separate add-ons.
cancel.gotchas: Downgrading removes professional monitoring and may shorten cloud video history. Check whether you are billed monthly or yearly before you switch, since a yearly term may run to its end date.

name: ADT
why: Professionally installed ADT runs on a 36-month contract (24 in California), and early termination can cost 75% of the remaining months. Negotiate near the contract end instead of cancelling mid-term.

alternatives.name: ADT Blu (no-contract tiers)
alternatives.note: ADT lists self-install plans without contracts, though a monthly plan is still required.

haggle.leverage: Your contract end date, published SimpliSafe and Ring Protect Pro prices, and ADT's own no-contract Blu DIY monitoring. Retention teams can sometimes offer a lower monthly rate or free equipment.
haggle.script: Hi, I've been an ADT customer for [X] years, and my contract ends on [date]. I'm paying $[amount] a month for monitoring. SimpliSafe and Ring both publish month-to-month plans that are meaningfully lower. I'd prefer to stay with ADT, so what rate can you offer if I renew? Please give me any offer in writing, including the contract length and the early termination terms. If you cannot lower the rate, please tell me the exact steps and date to end service without a penalty.
haggle.bestTime: In the 60 to 90 days before your contract ends, by phone, and ask for the retention or loyalty department.

cancel.howTo: Call ADT customer service and ask for your contract end date and exact payoff balance before you cancel. Ask them to confirm the cancellation and final bill in writing.
cancel.gotchas: ADT's terms say that ending a 36-month monitoring contract early can mean paying 75% of the monthly charges due for the rest of the term (California contracts are 24 months). Financed equipment keeps billing separately, so ask for both numbers.

name: Arlo Secure
why: Arlo cameras stream live and send basic alerts without a plan. Secure Plus runs $9.99 a month for one camera or $19.99 for unlimited. Pay only for cameras whose footage you actually review.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at my.arlo.com (or the Arlo app > Settings > Subscription), open Subscriptions, select the plan and cancel it.
cancel.gotchas: Plans are per camera or unlimited, and the Premium tier adds professional monitoring. Without a plan, cloud clips, AI detection and facial recognition stop, so download any clips you want to keep first.

name: Aura
why: Aura Individual is $12/mo billed annually ($15 monthly), with a 60-day refund window on annual plans. Free credit freezes cover the basics, so keep it only for the monitoring and recovery help. Never self-host this.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to Aura on the web or in the app, open Account > Subscription and cancel. If the option is missing, use chat or phone support from the Help page.
cancel.gotchas: Annual plans carry a 60-day money-back guarantee, and the free trial can be redeemed once per customer. The pricing page does not state the renewal price, so confirm it before the anniversary. Free credit freezes at the three bureaus stay in place after you cancel.

name: Backblaze Personal Backup
why: Unlimited off-site backup for one computer at $9/mo ($99 a year) is hard to beat, and a backup only counts if a copy sits off-site. Cancel only if another off-site copy already exists.

alternatives.name: Pay yearly or for two years
alternatives.note: $99 a year ($8.25/mo) or $189 for two years beats the $9 monthly rate.

cancel.howTo: Per Backblaze's help article: sign in at secure.backblaze.com, open Preferences, choose Delete Backup next to each computer, then open Overview and delete the unused license. Then check that your account shows no active renewal. If the steps differ, contact support before deleting anything.
cancel.gotchas: Deleting a backup removes its stored files at once and cannot be undone, so keep a local or other off-site copy first. Monthly plans are not refundable; yearly and two-year plans can be refunded within 30 days of subscribing. Forever version history is a paid add-on.

name: Bitwarden Premium
why: At $19.80 a year it is already the cheap option. Premium adds the built-in authenticator, file attachments, vault health reports and emergency access. Never rebuild or self-host a password manager.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to the web vault at vault.bitwarden.com, open Settings > Subscription and cancel Premium. Your vault stays on the free plan.
cancel.gotchas: Premium-only features end, including the integrated authenticator (TOTP), file attachments, vault health reports and emergency access. Move any 2FA codes held in Bitwarden to another authenticator before cancelling.

name: Blink Subscription Plan
why: Blink gives live view and motion alerts without a plan, and a USB drive in a Sync Module 2 can hold clips locally. Basic is $3.99 a month per device and Plus is $11.99 for unlimited devices.

cancel.howTo: Open the Blink app > Settings > Subscription Plans and cancel, or manage it in your Amazon account under Memberships and subscriptions if it was billed through Amazon.
cancel.gotchas: Plus bundles an extended warranty and device discounts that end with the plan. Check which features you use (cloud history, person detection) before cancelling, and confirm what the Sync Module 2 local option needs on your current plan.

name: Box (Personal Pro)
why: Personal Pro sells 100 GB, while iCloud+ sells 200 GB for $2.99 and Google One 100 GB for $1.99. Unless you need Box Sign or a work integration, move your files and drop the plan.

alternatives.name: iCloud+ 200 GB
alternatives.note: $2.99/mo for 200 GB, built into iPhone and Mac.

alternatives.name: Google One
alternatives.note: 100 GB at $1.99/mo, 15 GB free.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at box.com, open Account Settings, go to the plan or billing section and downgrade to the free Individual plan.
cancel.gotchas: The free Individual plan has 10 GB of storage and a 250 MB upload cap. Over 10 GB you must delete or move files. Download a full copy, including any older file versions you need, before you downgrade.

name: Dashlane
why: Dashlane sells yearly Premium and Friends & Family plans with a 14-day trial. A free Bitwarden vault covers the basics, so check you use the extras before you renew. Never self-host this.

alternatives.name: Bitwarden
alternatives.note: Free plan with unlimited passwords and devices; Premium is $19.80 a year.

cancel.howTo: If you paid by card on the Dashlane website, open the web app in a computer browser and cancel from the Vault menu (Plan or Subscription). If you paid through the Apple App Store, Google Play or PayPal, cancel there instead.
cancel.gotchas: Cancelling turns off auto-renewal, and you keep your plan and data until the current period ends. The in-app cancel option appears only in a browser, not in the mobile or Mac apps. Export your vault and choose a new manager before the plan ends.

name: Dropbox Plus
why: Plus is 2 TB for $9.99/mo billed yearly. Nextcloud or Syncthing replace the sync, but with the off-site copy counted, self-hosting pays only for a mid-sized library you do not share. Keep it if you send links.

alternatives.name: Syncthing
alternatives.note: Peer-to-peer folder sync between your own devices, no server or account.

alternatives.name: Dropbox Basic (free)
alternatives.note: 2 GB free tier, enough for a few shared folders.

selfhost.youLose: Dropbox apps that work everywhere with Smart Sync, shared links that anyone can open without a VPN, third-party integrations, and support. A dead disk means lost files unless you keep a second copy off-site. The cost figure counts about $38 a year of off-site bucket storage for 500 GB. A 2 TB library would cost about $167 a year at $6.95 per TB a month, more than the plan. A second disk is not counted.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. I want to replace my Dropbox Plus subscription with a self-hosted Nextcloud server for my own files. Target: an always-on old laptop or NAS running Ubuntu Server 24.04 with Docker (a Raspberry Pi 5 with an SSD also works). Walk me through: 1) a Docker Compose stack with the official Nextcloud image, Postgres and Redis, with data on its own disk, 2) a nightly restic backup to a second drive plus an encrypted off-site copy, 3) Tailscale on the server, phone and laptops with HTTPS through tailscale serve, so no router ports are opened, 4) the Nextcloud desktop and mobile clients with selective sync, 5) migrating by syncing Dropbox to a local folder, copying it into Nextcloud and comparing file counts and sizes. Explain how to share a file with a friend who is not on my tailnet and what that exposes. Finish with a restore test before I cancel.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at dropbox.com, open your profile menu > Settings > Plan, and choose Cancel plan. If you subscribed in the iOS or Android app, cancel in Apple Subscriptions or Google Play instead.
cancel.gotchas: You fall back to the free Basic plan (2 GB per the pricing page). If you hold more than that, Dropbox stops syncing new changes until you free space or upgrade, so move files first. The plan usually runs to the end of the period you paid for.

name: ecobee Smart Security
why: ecobee Smart Security now has Core (free), Plus ($5/mo) and Advanced ($10/mo) tiers. Existing pricing holds through December 2026 only if you change nothing, so check the new tier before you renew.

cancel.howTo: Use the ecobee app or your account on ecobee.com to open Smart Security subscription settings and cancel or downgrade the plan.
cancel.gotchas: ecobee says plan changes, add-on changes, cancellation or a lapse in service move you to current pricing and permanently end loyalty discounts. Professional monitoring is a separate add-on.

name: eufy Security Cloud Storage
why: eufy cameras record to local storage at no charge, and cloud storage ($2.99 per camera, or $9.99 for up to 10) is optional. Cancel unless you need off-site clips in case a camera is stolen.

cancel.howTo: Open the eufy Security app, go to your account or cloud storage subscription settings, and cancel the plan. If it was billed through Apple or Google, cancel there.
cancel.gotchas: Confirm that your cameras have a card or HomeBase drive recording locally before you cancel. Cloud clips stop being stored when the plan ends, so save any you need first.

name: ExpressVPN
why: The long Advanced plan shows $4.49/mo, but it renews at $119.95 a year (about $10/mo). Ask for a retention price before you renew; a home Tailscale exit node covers only public Wi-Fi and home access.

alternatives.name: Private Internet Access
alternatives.note: $47.88 a year, renewing at the same price.

haggle.leverage: ExpressVPN lists annual renewal at $99.95 (Basic), $119.95 (Advanced) and $199.95 (Pro), while rivals advertise multi-year plans near $2.50 to $3.50 a month and PIA charges $47.88 a year.
haggle.script: Hi, my ExpressVPN subscription renews on [date] at $119.95 for the year. I've been comparing providers, and several multi-year plans work out to a third of that, including Surfshark, and PIA charges $47.88 a year. I'd like to stay with ExpressVPN, so what is the best price you can offer me to renew, either for 12 months or on a longer plan? If there is a retention discount, please apply it to my account before I turn off auto-renewal, and send the confirmed total and renewal date in writing.
haggle.bestTime: A few days before the renewal date, through live chat from your account, before you switch off auto-renewal.

selfhost.youLose: Choice of countries, streaming-region access, hiding your home IP from websites, a no-logs claim backed by audits, and ExpressVPN extras such as its password manager and identity tools. You keep public Wi-Fi protection and access to home devices.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. I want to replace my ExpressVPN subscription with a Tailscale exit node at home for public Wi-Fi protection and access to my home devices. Target: an old laptop running Ubuntu Server 24.04 (a Raspberry Pi also works), wired to my router. Steps: 1) install Tailscale, enable IP forwarding, and advertise the machine as an exit node and as a subnet router for my home LAN, 2) approve the routes in the admin console and set key expiry and access controls for my own devices only, 3) install Tailscale on my phone and laptop and show me how to switch the exit node on and off, 4) add Pi-hole or AdGuard Home for DNS, 5) enable unattended OS upgrades and a nightly config backup. Provide exact commands and a test checklist for DNS leaks, IP leaks and speed. List plainly what I lose compared with ExpressVPN: country choice, streaming-region access and hiding my home IP.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to your ExpressVPN account on the website, open Subscription and turn off automatic renewal. Live chat can handle it too. If you subscribed through Apple or Google, cancel in that store.
cancel.gotchas: ExpressVPN offers a 30-day money-back guarantee for new users. Plans renew yearly at the full rate shown on the pricing page, far above the intro monthly figure. Higher tiers bundle extras you may be paying for elsewhere.

name: Flickr Pro
why: Pro is $82 a year ($11 monthly) for unlimited full-size storage, ad-free browsing and stats. As a private archive, Immich at home replaces it. If you share publicly or use the community, keep it.

alternatives.name: Immich
alternatives.note: Self-hosted private photo archive with mobile backup.

selfhost.youLose: The Flickr community, public pages with views and favorites, groups, ad-free sharing links and the off-site copy. You manage disks, backups and updates. The cost figure includes about $13 a year for an off-site copy of a typical 150 GB archive.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. I want to move my Flickr photo archive to a self-hosted Immich server and cancel Flickr Pro. Target: an always-on old laptop running Ubuntu Server 24.04 with Docker, or a NAS with Docker support. Walk me through: 1) installing Immich using the official docker-compose files and Postgres, 2) storing originals on a disk with a second copy and a nightly encrypted restic backup to an off-site bucket, 3) Tailscale on the server and my phone for remote access without open router ports, 4) requesting my Flickr data export, extracting the original files, and importing them with the Immich CLI while preserving capture dates (use exiftool to fix any missing dates from Flickr's JSON metadata), 5) recreating my main albums. Give exact commands, a count-match checklist before I cancel, and a restore test. Tell me which Flickr metadata (comments, favorites, groups) I will lose.

cancel.howTo: On the web: profile photo > Settings > Membership status > Manage your Pro subscription > Cancel your subscription. If you subscribed in the iOS or Android app: Flickr app > Profile > Settings > Flickr Pro > Manage subscription.
cancel.gotchas: Cancel at least a day before the billing date. Pro lasts until the term ends, then the account is free, capped at 1,000 items and 50 non-public photos or videos; content over the limits risks suspension or deletion. Export first (Settings > Your Flickr Data).

name: Google Nest Aware (Google Home Premium)
why: Nest Aware became Google Home Premium: Standard is $10/mo, Advanced $20. Google AI Pro already includes Standard, so check for double billing before paying separately.

cancel.howTo: Open the Google Home app > Settings > Subscriptions (Home Premium), choose the plan and cancel. If you bought through the Google Store, a Google One bundle or Apple, manage it there instead.
cancel.gotchas: Google AI Pro includes the Standard plan. If you pay for both, cancel the standalone one. Cameras lose cloud event history and the AI features, but live view and basic alerts remain.

name: Google One

priceHints.plan: Google One 200 GB (older Standard tier, still billed to existing members)
Google One 2 TB (also sold as Google AI Plus)

why: At $1.99 for 100 GB it is cheap, and it backs Gmail, Drive and Photos together. Self-hosting photos does not beat it once an off-site copy is counted. Trim usage or drop to the free 15 GB instead.

alternatives.name: Immich
alternatives.note: Self-hosted Google Photos replacement with mobile auto-backup.

alternatives.name: Google Takeout
alternatives.note: Official export of Photos, Drive and Gmail before you downgrade.

selfhost.youLose: Google Photos search, Memories and shared albums that anyone can open, Gmail and Drive headroom, and the off-site copy. You manage backups, updates and disk health yourself. The cost figure includes about $8 a year for an off-site copy of 100 GB.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. I want to replace Google Photos storage with a self-hosted Immich server so I can cancel my Google One plan or drop to the free tier. Target: an always-on old laptop running Ubuntu Server 24.04 with Docker, or a NAS with Docker. Walk me through: 1) installing Immich with the official docker-compose files and Postgres, 2) keeping the library on a disk with a second copy plus an encrypted nightly restic backup to an off-site bucket, 3) Tailscale on the server and my phone for remote access without open ports, 4) exporting everything with Google Takeout and importing it using immich-go so albums, dates and descriptions survive, 5) installing the Immich app on Android or iPhone with automatic backup. Include exact commands, a count-match checklist (photos, videos, albums) to finish before I delete anything from Google, and a restore drill from the backup.

cancel.howTo: Open one.google.com/settings, choose Cancel membership and confirm. On Android use the Google One app > Settings > Cancel membership. If you subscribed through Apple, cancel under Apple Subscriptions instead.
cancel.gotchas: You drop to 15 GB shared across Gmail, Drive and Photos. Over that, you cannot upload or receive new email, and Google says it may delete content in accounts that stay over quota for two years. Check you are not on a Google AI plan, which bills through the same page.

name: iCloud+
why: Plans run $0.99 (50 GB), $2.99 (200 GB) and $9.99 (2 TB) and hold device backups, Photos and Keychain. Self-hosting does not beat them once an off-site copy is counted, and it replaces only the photo library.

alternatives.name: Immich
alternatives.note: Self-hosted photo library with iPhone and Android auto-backup.

alternatives.name: Free 5 GB iCloud tier
alternatives.note: Enough for contacts, settings and a small backup if photos live elsewhere.

selfhost.youLose: iPhone device backups, iCloud Keychain, iMessage in iCloud, Shared Albums that non-technical relatives can open, and the built-in off-site copy. You become the backup admin, and one failed disk without a second copy loses photos. icloudpd does not work if Advanced Data Protection is on (use a privacy.apple.com export instead), and albums need one icloudpd run per album. The cost figure includes about $8 a year for an off-site copy of 100 GB.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. I want to move my iCloud Photos library to a self-hosted Immich server so I can drop my iCloud+ storage tier. Target: an always-on old laptop running Ubuntu Server 24.04 with Docker, or my NAS. First ask whether Advanced Data Protection is on: icloudpd does not work with it, so tell me to request a full export from privacy.apple.com or turn it off for the migration. Then: 1) install Immich from the official docker-compose files with Postgres, 2) keep the library on a disk with a second copy, plus a nightly encrypted restic job to an off-site bucket, 3) install Tailscale on the server and my phone, 4) list my albums, run icloudpd once per album with --album into a folder per album, and upload each folder with immich upload --album, 5) turn on automatic backup in the Immich iPhone app. Give exact commands, a photo and video count checklist before I downgrade, and a restore test.

cancel.howTo: iPhone or iPad: Settings > your name > Subscriptions > iCloud+ > Cancel Subscription, or Settings > your name > iCloud > Manage Account Storage > Change Storage Plan > Downgrade Options. Mac: System Settings > your name > iCloud > Manage > Change Storage Plan. You can also use account.apple.com.
cancel.gotchas: The free tier is 5 GB. If you are over it, device backups and Photos uploads pause until you free space or resubscribe. Download your photos first (Photos settings > Download and Keep Originals, or a data export at privacy.apple.com). Family Sharing members lose a shared plan too.

name: Keeper Password Manager
why: Keeper bills per year, with BreachWatch dark-web monitoring and extra file storage as paid add-ons. Check you are not paying for add-ons you never use. Never rebuild or self-host a password manager.

alternatives.name: Bitwarden
alternatives.note: Free plan with unlimited passwords and devices.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to the Keeper web vault, open your account and subscription settings, and turn off auto-renewal or remove the add-ons. Store-billed subscriptions are cancelled in Apple or Google.
cancel.gotchas: The personal and family plans bill yearly and renew automatically, and BreachWatch and storage are separate add-ons. Export your records before the plan lapses.

name: LastPass
why: LastPass Free is limited to one device type; Premium lifts that. After the breaches LastPass disclosed in 2022, compare Bitwarden or 1Password before renewing by default. Never rebuild or self-host this.

alternatives.name: Bitwarden
alternatives.note: Free plan with unlimited passwords and devices; Premium is $19.80 a year.

cancel.howTo: Log in to the LastPass web vault, open Account Settings > Billing (or Manage Subscription) and cancel Premium, Families or Plus. Store-billed subscriptions are cancelled in Apple or Google.
cancel.gotchas: The free plan works on one device type only (computers or mobile), so downgrading breaks sync between your laptop and phone. Export your vault before cancelling and delete the old copy once you have moved it.

name: LifeLock
why: LifeLock plans are sold on a first-year promotion and renew at a higher rate, so ask for the loyalty price before renewal. Free credit freezes at the three bureaus cover the core protection.

haggle.leverage: First-year versus renewal pricing, competing identity services such as Aura, free credit freezes, and the 60-day refund window on annual plans.
haggle.script: Hi, my LifeLock membership renews on [date] at $[price]. New customers pay much less in their first year, and I'm comparing Aura and the free credit freezes at the credit bureaus. I'd like to stay, so can you apply a loyalty or first-year rate to my renewal? Please tell me the exact price, the term and the date it renews, and confirm it by email. If there is no discount available, please turn off auto-renewal and confirm the cancellation in writing.
haggle.bestTime: One to two weeks before the renewal date, by phone, and ask for the retention department.

cancel.howTo: Sign in to your LifeLock or Norton account, open the membership and turn off auto-renewal, or contact Member Services to cancel. If you bought Norton 360 with LifeLock, cancel in your Norton account.
cancel.gotchas: Annual plans advertise a 60-day money-back guarantee, and the site says you can cancel anytime. Turn off auto-renewal before the anniversary to avoid a charge at the higher regular rate.

name: Malwarebytes Premium
why: Malwarebytes Premium (listed around $44.99 a year for one device) duplicates the protection built into Windows and macOS for most home users. Keep it only if you rely on its scanning or VPN extras.

alternatives.name: Microsoft Defender
alternatives.note: Built into Windows at no cost.

alternatives.name: Malwarebytes Free
alternatives.note: Free on-demand scanner.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at my.malwarebytes.com, open Subscriptions and turn off auto-renew. If it was billed through Apple or Google, cancel there.
cancel.gotchas: Plans bill yearly and renew at the regular rate. Security.org reports a 60-day refund window, but check the one shown at checkout. Deactivate the app on each device after you cancel.

name: McAfee+
why: McAfee often arrives as a preinstalled trial that auto-renews, and intro prices jump on renewal (one plan goes from $29.99 to $84.99). Windows and macOS already include baseline protection.

alternatives.name: Microsoft Defender
alternatives.note: Built into Windows at no cost.

haggle.leverage: The renewal price versus the first-year price, built-in alternatives, and the fact that McAfee often runs auto-renew promotions for existing customers.
haggle.script: Hi, my McAfee subscription is set to renew on [date] at $[price]. That is much higher than the first-year price, and I'm comparing it with the protection already built into my computer. I'd keep McAfee if you can offer a loyalty or first-year price for the next term. Can you apply any available discount today, and confirm the new total, the term length and the date it renews in writing? If not, please cancel auto-renewal and confirm that by email.
haggle.bestTime: At least a week before the renewal date, by chat or phone, before turning off auto-renewal.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at mcafee.com > My Account, open your subscription and turn off automatic renewal. Chat support can finish the cancellation. If it was billed through Apple or Google, cancel there.
cancel.gotchas: Refund windows are short, so cancel before the renewal date rather than after. Trials need cancelling about seven days before they end. Some bundles tie VPN features to auto-renew or sign you up for two years, so read the terms.

name: Microsoft OneDrive (100 GB)
why: The 100 GB tier is Microsoft 365 Basic at $1.99/mo ($19.99/yr), one of the cheapest storage plans. Drop it only if you can stay under the free 5 GB, and check you do not also pay for Microsoft 365 Personal or Family.

alternatives.name: OneDrive free tier
alternatives.note: 5 GB free with a Microsoft account.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at account.microsoft.com/services, find the Microsoft 365 Basic (or OneDrive) subscription, choose Manage > Cancel subscription, and confirm.
cancel.gotchas: The 100 GB tier is a Microsoft 365 plan, so cancelling can also remove ad-free Outlook and other Basic extras. If you are over the free 5 GB after it ends, OneDrive goes read-only: you can view and download but not upload. Move files before the end date.

name: NordVPN
why: NordVPN sells deep multi-year discounts, then renews at the standard rate, so the renewal date is when to push for a retention offer. A home WireGuard server covers public Wi-Fi and home access only.

alternatives.name: Surfshark
alternatives.note: Advertises 24-month plans from about $2.49/mo.

alternatives.name: Private Internet Access
alternatives.note: $47.88 a year, renewing at the same price.

haggle.leverage: Your renewal date, and rival multi-year prices: Surfshark advertises 24-month plans from about $2.49 a month, ExpressVPN's 28-month Basic plan is $2.99 a month, and PIA charges $47.88 a year.
haggle.script: Hi, I'm a NordVPN subscriber and my plan renews on [date]. The renewal price is well above the multi-year deals other providers advertise, such as Surfshark at about $2.49 a month and ExpressVPN at about $2.99 a month. I'd like to stay, so what is the best price you can give me to renew for the next 12 or 24 months? If there is a retention discount or coupon, please apply it before I turn off auto-renew, and confirm the exact total and billing date in writing.
haggle.bestTime: A week or two before the renewal date, through live chat from your account, and be ready to turn off auto-renew if the offer is weak.

selfhost.youLose: IP addresses in other countries, streaming-region access, hiding your location from websites (your home IP is exposed), multi-hop and malware-blocking features, and any support. It covers public Wi-Fi protection and access to your home network.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. I want to replace my NordVPN subscription with a self-hosted WireGuard VPN at home, mainly for safer public Wi-Fi and reaching my home network. Target: a Raspberry Pi 4 or newer (or an old laptop) running Raspberry Pi OS Lite or Ubuntu Server, wired to my router. Set up: 1) WireGuard with PiVPN, 2) a dynamic DNS name and one UDP port forward, or Tailscale with the server as an exit node if my ISP uses CGNAT, 3) client configs and QR codes for my phone and laptop, with automatic connection on untrusted Wi-Fi, 4) Pi-hole on the same box for DNS ad blocking, 5) unattended OS updates and a backup of the config. Give exact commands and a test checklist (DNS leak test, speed test, reconnect after a reboot), plus an honest list of what I lose compared with NordVPN, including other countries' IP addresses and region unblocking.

cancel.howTo: Log in to your Nord Account, open the Billing tab, click Cancel next to auto-renewal and confirm; a confirmation email follows. If you subscribed through Google Play, the Apple App Store or the Amazon Appstore, cancel in that store instead.
cancel.gotchas: Multi-year plans are charged up front, and renewal uses the then-current rate, which can be far above your intro price. All plans carry a 30-day money-back guarantee. NordPass and NordLocker are separate subscriptions on the same account.

name: Norton 360

priceHints.plan: Norton 360 Deluxe, renewal (reported by some reviews)

why: First-year prices are promotional: Deluxe is $49.99 and renews at $124.99, per security.org. Call before renewal for a retention price, or cancel if Microsoft Defender or macOS protection is enough.

alternatives.name: Microsoft Defender
alternatives.note: Built into Windows at no cost.

haggle.leverage: The gap between the first-year price and the renewal price, a built-in alternative (Microsoft Defender), and the 60-day refund window on annual plans.
haggle.script: Hi, my Norton 360 subscription renews on [date] at $[renewal price], which is far above what new customers pay in their first year. Windows already includes Microsoft Defender, so I'm deciding whether to keep paying. I'd stay with Norton if you can match the first-year promotional price for another year. Can you apply that offer or a retention discount today? Please confirm the new price, the term and the renewal date in writing by email. If there is no discount, I'll cancel before the renewal date.
haggle.bestTime: One to two weeks before renewal, by phone or chat, and ask for retention; after the renewal charge you are limited to the 60-day refund window.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at my.norton.com, open your subscription and turn off automatic renewal (or cancel). Support chat or phone can process it. Store-billed plans are cancelled in Apple or Google.
cancel.gotchas: Annual plans renew automatically at the higher regular rate. Norton advertises a 60-day money-back guarantee on annual plans, so cancel within 60 days of a charge to get it back. Expect retention offers, and note LifeLock bundles are cancelled separately.

name: Plex Pass
why: Since April 2025, streaming your own server away from home needs Plex Pass or a Remote Watch Pass. Jellyfin on the same hardware does it free over Tailscale, but you lose Plex polish and its apps.

alternatives.name: Jellyfin
alternatives.note: Free, open-source media server with no paid tier.

selfhost.youLose: Plex's polished apps on every TV, its free ad-supported catalog, Watchlist and Discover, easy friend sharing, and its metadata matching. Jellyfin TV apps vary by platform, and friends need accounts plus a way to reach your server. The cost figure is zero because the machine already runs Plex.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. I want to replace Plex Pass with Jellyfin on the machine that already hosts my Plex library. Target: an always-on spare PC, old laptop or NAS running Ubuntu Server 24.04 with Docker. Walk me through: 1) installing Jellyfin with Docker, mounting media read-only so Plex keeps running during the trial, 2) Movies, TV Shows and Music libraries with correct naming, 3) hardware transcoding if my GPU supports it, 4) Tailscale on the server and clients for remote playback with no router ports, 5) a nightly backup of Jellyfin's config and data folders, 6) family accounts and watched-status migration with JellyPlex-Watched. Ask which TVs and streamers I own and check each against jellyfin.org/downloads/clients: Apple TV, Android TV, Fire TV, Roku and LG webOS have clients, Samsung has a Tizen client so check my model, and tell me what to do for any device without one. End with a checklist so I cancel Plex Pass only after playback, subtitles and remote streaming work.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at plex.tv, open Account > Subscription & Payments, choose Manage on the Plex Pass subscription, then cancel automatic renewal. If you subscribed through an app store (Apple, Google Play, Amazon or Roku), cancel there.
cancel.gotchas: You keep Plex Pass until the paid period ends, with no refund for unused time. Without it, remote streaming from your server needs a Remote Watch Pass for each viewer (Plex lists $2.99 a month or $29.99 a year from June 2026). A lifetime Plex Pass is a one-time purchase with nothing to cancel.

name: Private Internet Access (PIA)
why: $47.88 a year renewing at the same price is cheap. A home WireGuard server saves under $42 a year and replaces neither server choice nor hiding your home IP, so keep PIA unless you only need remote access to home.

selfhost.youLose: Servers in dozens of countries, region unblocking, port forwarding through the provider for torrents, and hiding your home IP from websites. Savings are small: the plan is about $48 a year.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. I want to replace Private Internet Access with a WireGuard server on a Raspberry Pi at home. Target: Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 running Raspberry Pi OS Lite 64-bit on Ethernet, with a reserved IP on my router. Steps: 1) install WireGuard with PiVPN, creating profiles for my phone and laptop, 2) a dynamic DNS name and one UDP port forward, or Tailscale as the fallback if my ISP uses CGNAT, 3) a kill switch on my laptop client so traffic stops if the tunnel drops, 4) unattended upgrades and a backup of the WireGuard config and an SD card image, 5) a verification pass: DNS leak test, IPv6 leak test, speed test and a reboot test. Be explicit about what I lose compared with PIA, such as country choice and provider port forwarding, and tell me how to decide whether the roughly $48 a year saved is worth the upkeep.

cancel.howTo: Log in to your PIA Client Control Panel, find Next Billing and select Turn off auto-renewal, then confirm. Your account stays active until the paid term ends. Subscriptions bought through the Apple App Store or Google Play are cancelled in that store.
cancel.gotchas: The 3-year plan auto-renews at $79 every 3 years, so a charge can land years after you forget. A 30-day money-back guarantee applies to new subscribers; subscriptions bought through app stores follow the store refund terms.

name: Proton (Unlimited, VPN, Mail, Pass)
why: Unlimited is $9.99/mo billed yearly and bundles VPN, Mail, Drive, Pass and Calendar. It can replace several separate subscriptions, so cancel overlapping standalone ones first.

alternatives.name: Proton Free
alternatives.note: Free tier for Mail, Calendar, Drive and VPN with limits.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at account.proton.me, open Settings > Dashboard (Subscription) and cancel or downgrade to Free. If you subscribed through Apple or Google, cancel in that store.
cancel.gotchas: Yearly billing runs to the end of the paid year. After downgrade, paid VPN servers, custom domains and extra storage end, and an account over the free storage limit can be restricted until you free space. Export mail and Drive files first.

name: Ring Protect
why: Ring cameras keep live view and alerts without a plan. Recording and history need Solo ($4.99), Multi ($9.99) or Pro ($19.99). Keep it if you review footage; otherwise step down to Solo or cancel.

alternatives.name: eufy cameras with local storage
alternatives.note: Record to a built-in card or drive with no subscription; cloud storage is optional.

cancel.howTo: In the Ring app open the menu and go to your Ring Protect plan settings (or sign in at ring.com and open your account), select the location, then choose Cancel plan or change to Solo. Menu names shift between app versions.
cancel.gotchas: Plans are per location, and Multi and Pro cover every device there. Ring lists plans as auto-renewing until canceled and starts a 30-day trial when you set up a device, so cancel before day 30 if you do not want it. Pro includes 24/7 professional monitoring, which stops with the plan.

name: SimpliSafe
why: Plans are month-to-month with no contract, so leaving is a real threat. Core is $32.99, Standard $22.99 (no camera recordings) and Self-Monitoring $9.99. Ask for a loyalty rate or step down a tier.

alternatives.name: Ring Protect Pro
alternatives.note: $19.99/mo with 24/7 professional monitoring at one location.

haggle.leverage: No contract, so you can leave any month. Credible alternatives: SimpliSafe Standard at $22.99 or Self-Monitoring at $9.99, or Ring Protect Pro at $19.99 a month with professional monitoring.
haggle.script: Hi, I've been a SimpliSafe customer for a few years on the Core plan at $32.99 a month. I'm reviewing my monthly costs and comparing alternatives, including Ring's Pro plan at $19.99 a month. I'd rather stay, so I'm asking whether there is a loyalty rate or promotional price available on Core. If not, could you tell me exactly what I would lose by moving to Standard at $22.99, and whether camera recordings could be kept on a separate cheaper plan? I'd like to decide today if there is an offer.
haggle.bestTime: Weekday morning by phone or chat, ideally right after a price increase or after a quiet stretch with no alarm events.

cancel.howTo: Chat with SimpliSafe support or call 1-888-783-8441 to cancel or change your monitoring plan. In some states you can start a cancellation online: SimpliSafe.com Account > Security Dashboard > Manage Account. Only the account owner can cancel.
cancel.gotchas: Plans are billed monthly with no contract. Without a monitoring plan you lose 24/7 dispatch, though live camera video and remote arming stay in the app. Self-Monitoring at $9.99 keeps 30 days of recordings for up to 10 cameras but no professional monitoring. Sales tax may apply.

name: SmugMug
why: At $23.50/mo billed yearly it earns its keep if you sell prints or deliver client galleries. For a plain portfolio of your own photos, a static site you generate yourself does the job.

alternatives.name: Cloudflare Pages
alternatives.note: Free static hosting for a portfolio built with Astro or Eleventy.

rebuild.whatYouBuild: A static photo portfolio generated from folders of images: album pages, responsive grid, keyboard-friendly lightbox, build-time resized WebP images, EXIF captions, unlisted albums and a sitemap.
rebuild.runsOn: Static site built on your own machine with Astro, then uploaded with Wrangler to Cloudflare Pages (free tier) on your own domain. Originals stay on your disk and out of Git.
rebuild.youLose: Print and merchandise sales, client proofing and download delivery, unlimited original-file storage and its off-site backup, password-protected galleries, analytics and support. Keep SmugMug if clients or print sales matter.
rebuild.prompt: Build me a static photo portfolio website to replace my SmugMug plan. Stack: Astro with plain CSS and no database. Features: 1) a home page with a featured grid, 2) album pages generated from folders under photos/<album>/, each with a responsive masonry grid and a keyboard-accessible lightbox, 3) a build script using sharp that creates WebP thumbnails and 2000px display sizes, 4) captions and alt text read from a per-album YAML file plus EXIF data, 5) unlisted albums with long random URLs, left out of navigation and the sitemap, with noindex meta tags and a robots rule, and tell me they are unlisted, not private, 6) a contact page with a mailto link. Add an import script that turns a folder of originals downloaded from SmugMug into one album per folder. Build on my machine so the originals never go into Git, and publish the built dist folder to the Cloudflare Pages free tier with Wrangler on my custom domain. Include a README and state the file-count and file-size limits I will hit.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at smugmug.com, open Account Settings > Billing (or Subscription) and cancel the plan. Annual plans normally run to the end of the paid term.
cancel.gotchas: Download your originals first, because galleries, shop links and shared URLs go offline when the plan ends. SmugMug advertises a 14-day free trial, so cancel before it ends if you are only testing. The listed prices are per month but billed annually.

name: Surfshark
why: Surfshark advertises two-year plans near $2.49/mo, billed up front, then charges annually after. The renewal price is not shown on the pricing page, so check it and ask for a retention offer.

alternatives.name: Private Internet Access
alternatives.note: $47.88 a year, renewing at the same price.

haggle.leverage: Your renewal date and the gap between the advertised two-year deal and the renewal charge, plus PIA at $47.88 a year and ExpressVPN's 28-month Basic plan at $2.99 a month.
haggle.script: Hi, my Surfshark subscription renews on [date]. I originally signed up for a two-year deal at around $2.49 a month, and I want to know the exact renewal charge before it happens. I'm comparing PIA at $47.88 a year and ExpressVPN's long plans. I'd like to stay, so can you offer a retention price for the next 12 or 24 months, or move me onto the current promotional plan? Please confirm the total, the billing date and the term in writing before I decide whether to turn off auto-renewal.
haggle.bestTime: About a week before the renewal date, through live chat from your account.

selfhost.youLose: Servers in other countries, region unblocking, multi-hop, hiding your home IP from websites, and support. If your ISP uses carrier-grade NAT, a plain port forward will not work and you need Tailscale instead.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. I want to stop paying for Surfshark and run my own WireGuard VPN at home using wg-easy. Target: an old laptop on Ubuntu Server 24.04 with Docker, connected by Ethernet. Walk me through: 1) installing Docker and wg-easy with a docker-compose file and a strong admin password, 2) a dynamic DNS name (DuckDNS or Cloudflare) and the single UDP port forward on my router, with a fallback using Tailscale if my ISP uses CGNAT, 3) creating clients for my phone and laptop with QR codes and automatic connection on untrusted Wi-Fi, 4) firewall rules, automatic updates, and a backup of the WireGuard config, 5) DNS through AdGuard Home. Include a leak-test checklist and be explicit about what I give up compared with Surfshark: servers in other countries, region unblocking, multi-hop and hiding my home IP address.

cancel.howTo: Log in to your Surfshark account, click your email address (top right) > Subscription > Payments > Cancel auto-renewal, then confirm. Live chat can also cancel it. If you subscribed through Google Play, the Apple App Store or the Amazon Appstore, cancel in that store.
cancel.gotchas: Cancelling auto-renewal keeps access until the end of the paid period. Surfshark says two-year plans are billed once at the start and then annually after they expire, and the renewal amount is not listed on the pricing page. A 30-day money-back guarantee applies to new subscriptions.

name: Tile Premium
why: Tile Premium adds extras such as smart alerts and location history on top of the free tracker app. If you rarely lose things or already use Apple Find My or Google's tracker network, it is an easy cut.

cancel.howTo: Cancel where you subscribed. iPhone: Settings > your name > Subscriptions > Tile. Android: Play Store > Profile > Payments & subscriptions > Tile. Tile account on the Life360 website: log in, Account icon > Billing & Premium > Manage Subscription > Cancel Subscription.
cancel.gotchas: Refunds are not available for unused time, and benefits last to the end of the period. Premium Protect is a separate Tile tier, and Life360 family membership is a separate subscription, so cancel the right one. Trackers keep working with the free app.

name: Vivint
why: Vivint pairs a monitoring plan with equipment, often financed. Cancelling early can leave the remaining equipment balance due, so negotiate rate or term at renewal rather than walking away mid-contract.

haggle.leverage: A contract nearing its end, published SimpliSafe, Ring and ADT prices, and the fact that Vivint advertises month-to-month service when equipment is bought upfront.
haggle.script: Hi, I've been a Vivint customer for [X] years and I'm currently paying $[amount] a month for monitoring. I've compared SimpliSafe and Ring, whose published plans are lower and don't require long contracts. I'd like to stay, so what retention rate can you offer on my current service level, and can I move to month-to-month after my equipment is paid off? Please also tell me my remaining equipment balance and contract end date, and send any offer in writing so I can compare it before I decide.
haggle.bestTime: Within three months of your agreement ending, by phone, and ask for the retention team.

cancel.howTo: Call Vivint and ask for your agreement end date and the payoff balance on any financed equipment before you cancel. Ask for confirmation in writing.
cancel.gotchas: Vivint says that without a service plan, product functionality is limited, including loss of remote connectivity. Equipment financing is a separate agreement with a lender and keeps billing after monitoring ends.

name: Wyze Cam Plus
why: Cam Plus is $29.99 per camera per year. Frigate on an old laptop replaces it only for older models with RTSP firmware, and it pays only with 3 or more cameras. With one or two, keep Cam Plus on the front door camera.

alternatives.name: Local microSD recording
alternatives.note: Many Wyze cameras record continuously to a microSD card with no plan.

selfhost.youLose: Cam Plus detection tuned to Wyze hardware, simple cloud clips that survive a stolen camera, app polish and support. Only Wyze Cam v2, v3 and Pan v1 have RTSP firmware, and Wyze does not actively maintain it. Newer models cannot join. You manage disks and updates.
selfhost.prompt: I am running you on the target machine (or over SSH to it); confirm that before changing anything. I want to replace Wyze Cam Plus with Frigate NVR running locally. This only pays off with 3 or more cameras, so ask how many I have first; with one or two, tell me to keep Cam Plus on the front door camera. Target: an old x86 laptop (8 GB RAM) on Ubuntu Server 24.04 with Docker, plus a surveillance disk. Only Wyze Cam v2, v3 and Pan v1 have RTSP firmware, so ask for my camera models and tell me which can be used. Walk me through: 1) installing the RTSP firmware from a microSD card and putting each camera on an isolated IoT network, 2) a Frigate docker-compose setup using the sub-stream for detection and the main stream for recording, 3) person, car and pet detection on CPU or OpenVINO, 4) phone notifications through Home Assistant, 5) Tailscale for remote viewing. Include disk sizing math and an honest comparison with Cam Plus detection.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at my.wyze.com/account/services (or Wyze app > Account > Services), select Cam Plus, then Manage Subscription to cancel or reduce the number of cameras. If you subscribed through Apple, Google or Amazon, cancel there instead.
cancel.gotchas: Cam Plus is per camera, so keep it only on the doorbell or front door camera. Annual Cam Plus rose from $19.99 to $29.99 for renewals on or after March 2, 2026. Pro AI is a separate $4.99 per camera per month add-on with its own cancel button.

name: Amazon Music Unlimited
why: Prime members pay $11.99 for Unlimited, and Prime already includes Amazon Music with a smaller catalog, which is enough for some listeners. Keep it only if it is your main service; drop it if you also pay for another.

alternatives.name: Amazon Music with Prime
alternatives.note: Included with Prime at no extra cost, with a smaller catalog than Unlimited.

cancel.howTo: In Amazon Music settings open Amazon Music Unlimited and choose Cancel subscription, or use Memberships and Subscriptions in your Amazon account.
cancel.gotchas: The charge lives in your Amazon account, so it can hide among Prime renewals. Check the renewal date in Memberships and Subscriptions. After you cancel you keep access until the paid period ends.

name: AMC+
why: AMC+ is mostly Walking Dead and Anne Rice universe shows plus AMC series. Premium is $10.99, with an ads tier at $7.99. Subscribe when a series you follow airs, and note that Philo Bundle+ already includes it.

alternatives.name: Philo Bundle+
alternatives.note: $33 includes AMC+, HBO Max Basic with Ads and discovery+.

alternatives.name: Tubi
alternatives.note: Free ad-supported movies and TV.

rotate.pattern: Subscribe the months a series you follow airs, finish it, cancel. The ads tier is $7.99 if you can accept ads.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at amcplus.com, open Account, choose Manage Subscription and Cancel. If you joined through Amazon Channels, Apple, Roku or a TV provider, cancel there.
cancel.gotchas: The site shows several overlapping prices, so check what checkout charges. A 7-day free trial converts to paid. Annual Premium ($109.99) is paid up front.

name: Apple Arcade
why: A catalog of ad-free mobile games at $6.99 that people subscribe to once and forget. Play through what you want in a month or two, cancel, and rejoin when new games arrive.

alternatives.name: Apple One
alternatives.note: Includes Arcade with Music, TV and iCloud+ from $21.95.

rotate.pattern: Subscribe for a month or two, play the games you wanted, cancel, and rejoin when new titles land. Use the 3 free months that come with an eligible new device first.

cancel.howTo: iPhone or iPad: Settings > your name > Subscriptions > Apple Arcade > Cancel Subscription. Mac: App Store > your name > Subscriptions. Web: account.apple.com > Subscriptions.
cancel.gotchas: Games stop opening once the paid period ends. If the charge is part of Apple One, cancel or change Apple One instead.

name: Apple Music
why: A solid default if you live on Apple devices. Cancel it if you already pay for Spotify or YouTube Premium; two music subscriptions are rarely used equally. Apple One can be cheaper if you also use Apple TV.

alternatives.name: Apple One
alternatives.note: Individual $21.95 includes Music, TV, Arcade and 50 GB iCloud+.

alternatives.name: Apple Music Student
alternatives.note: $6.99 for verified college students.

cancel.howTo: iPhone or iPad: Settings > your name > Subscriptions > Apple Music > Cancel Subscription. Mac: App Store > your name > Subscriptions. Web: account.apple.com > Subscriptions.
cancel.gotchas: Songs you downloaded from the Apple Music catalog and library additions stop working when the subscription ends; music you bought or uploaded stays. If you pay for Apple One, cancel the bundle rather than Apple Music alone.

name: Apple One
why: Apple One only saves money if you use at least two of its services: Individual is $21.95 against $34.96 bought separately, per Apple. If you use one service plus iCloud, single plans can cost less.

alternatives.name: Apple Music alone
alternatives.note: $11.99 a month.

alternatives.name: Apple TV alone
alternatives.note: $14.99 a month.

cancel.howTo: iPhone or iPad: Settings > your name > Subscriptions > Apple One > Cancel Subscription. Mac: App Store > your name > Subscriptions. Web: account.apple.com > Subscriptions.
cancel.gotchas: Cancelling Apple One also drops its iCloud+ storage back to the free tier unless you buy a standalone plan, so back up first. Family and Premier need Family Sharing set up.

name: Apple TV (Apple TV+)
why: Apple TV has a small library and its fourth price hike since 2022 landed in August 2026. Shows come in short seasons, so one or two paid months a year usually covers what you want.

alternatives.name: Apple TV with a new device
alternatives.note: 3 months included when you buy an eligible Apple device.

alternatives.name: Apple One
alternatives.note: Cheaper than Apple TV plus Music if you use both.

rotate.pattern: Subscribe when a new season of a show you follow drops, finish it, then cancel right away. You keep access to the end of the paid month. Use device-purchase free months first.

cancel.howTo: iPhone or iPad: Settings > your name > Subscriptions > Apple TV > Cancel Subscription. Mac: App Store > your name > Subscriptions. Web: account.apple.com > Subscriptions.
cancel.gotchas: Cancel at least 24 hours before a free trial ends. If there is no Cancel button, it is already cancelled. If the charge comes from Apple One, cancel or change Apple One instead.

name: Audible
why: Audible makes sense if you use a credit every month and want to keep the books. If credits pile up unused you are prepaying. A library card through Libby gets many of the same titles free.

alternatives.name: Libby (public library)
alternatives.note: Free ebooks and audiobooks with a library card.

alternatives.name: Hoopla
alternatives.note: Free with a library card: audiobooks, comics, music and some video, with a monthly borrow limit.

alternatives.name: Audible Standard
alternatives.note: $8.99 a month for one selection that does not roll over, per Audible. Check whether titles stay after you cancel.

rotate.pattern: Use up your credits, cancel, and rejoin when you want the next batch of books. Audible says credits expire when a membership is cancelled, so spend them first. Check the rule for Standard before choosing it.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at audible.com, open Account Details, choose Cancel membership and click through the retention screens to the final confirmation.
cancel.gotchas: Spend unused credits first, since they can be lost when a membership ends. The cancel flow shows discounts and pause offers before the final screen. Intro offers ($0.99 a month for 3 months on the site) renew at the regular price.

name: BritBox
why: Most BritBox subscribers want one or two series. At about $10.99 a month, pay for a few months, watch them and leave. The annual plan is roughly 17% cheaper but ties up $109.99.

alternatives.name: Kanopy
alternatives.note: Free film streaming through many public libraries and universities, with a deep arthouse and classics selection.

alternatives.name: Tubi
alternatives.note: Free ad-supported movies and TV.

rotate.pattern: Subscribe for the months a series you want is available, finish it, cancel. Rejoin when the next one arrives.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at britbox.com, open your account, go to Subscription and choose Cancel. If billed through Apple, Amazon Channels or Roku, cancel there.
cancel.gotchas: An annual plan is paid up front. A free trial converts to paid unless cancelled before it ends.

name: Crunchyroll
why: Anime runs in four seasons a year. Fan at $9.99 (up $2 in 2026) covers most viewers, and Mega Fan adds more streams. Pay for the one or two seasons you follow and skip the rest.

alternatives.name: HIDIVE
alternatives.note: Another anime service, useful for titles that are not on Crunchyroll.

alternatives.name: Tubi
alternatives.note: Free ad-supported movies and TV.

rotate.pattern: Pay for the one or two simulcast seasons you follow, catch up on backlog during those months, and cancel between seasons.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at crunchyroll.com, open Account > Membership and choose Cancel Membership.
cancel.gotchas: If you subscribed through Apple, Google, Amazon, PlayStation or another partner, cancel there. Crunchyroll ended its free ad-supported tier at the end of 2025, so cancelling ends access entirely. Fan allows 1 device at a time.

name: DAZN
why: DAZN sells fight nights and season passes, and its cheaper monthly rate usually means a 12-month commitment. Pay monthly for the event or season you want and avoid annual-paid-monthly billing.

alternatives.name: Free DAZN account
alternatives.note: A free sign-up gives some free channels and games, depending on rights.

rotate.pattern: Take the monthly plan only for the months with the fights or games you want. Skip the annual-paid-monthly option; it keeps billing for 12 payments.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at dazn.com, open your account, go to Subscription and choose Cancel. The help center explains notice periods for each plan.
cancel.gotchas: DAZN's pricing page describes the monthly boxing plan as cancelable with 30 days' notice. An annual plan paid monthly commits you to 12 payments. If billed through Fubo, Apple or Google, cancel there.

name: discovery+
why: A thin catalog that overlaps with other services: Philo Bundle+ includes it, and it rose to $6.99 with ads and $11.99 ad-free in October 2026. Subscribe for a show you want, then drop it.

alternatives.name: HBO Max Basic with Ads
alternatives.note: $10.99 a month, a larger catalog from the same parent company.

alternatives.name: Tubi
alternatives.note: Free ad-supported movies and TV.

rotate.pattern: Subscribe for the month of a specific show, binge it and cancel. If you already pay for Philo Bundle+ or another service that carries it, skip it.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at discoveryplus.com, open your profile, go to Account then Manage Subscription and choose Cancel. If billed through Amazon, Apple, Roku or a TV provider, cancel there.
cancel.gotchas: The October 13, 2026 increase reached new subscribers first, with existing members getting 30 days notice. It may also be included in plans you already pay for, such as Philo Bundle+.

name: Disney+
why: Most households watch Disney+ in bursts around a release or a trip. Monthly billing makes dropping it between releases cheap, while the annual Premium plan commits $214.99 up front.

alternatives.name: Disney+ with ads
alternatives.note: $12.49 a month, $9 less than Premium.

rotate.pattern: Subscribe the month a Marvel, Star Wars or Pixar title lands or the kids need a movie weekend, then cancel. Stay on monthly billing rather than annual.

cancel.howTo: Sign in at disneyplus.com, open Account, select your subscription, and choose Cancel Subscription, then confirm.
cancel.gotchas: If you pay through Apple, Google, Amazon, Roku or a carrier, cancel there. Bundle discounts end if you drop one service. Annual plans are paid up front, so confirm how Disney treats the unused months before switching to one.

name: ESPN Select (ESPN+) and ESPN Unlimited
why: ESPN+ became ESPN Select at $13.99, with ESPN Unlimited at $31.99 after the September 2026 increases. Its value is live college and niche sports, so pay during the seasons you follow.

alternatives.name: Disney+, Hulu and ESPN Select bundle
